source: Dionysii Cartusiani Opera Omnia, t. X (Montreuil)

1.title: Elucidatio litteralis capituli primi: In mense octavo, in anno secundo Darii regis.
1.title_en: Literal explanation of the first chapter: In the eighth month, in the second year of Darius the king.

paras.t: Sicut sanctus ait Hieronymus, inter duodecim Prophetas obscurissimus est Zacharias, cujus nunc, Deo illustrante, elucidandus est liber. In proœmio autem suo Propheta iste aperuit, quo tempore cœperit prophetare. In mense octavo, in anno secundo, id est octavo mense anni secundi imperii Darii regis Persarum : de quo in exordio expositionis Aggæi prophetæ jam dictum est; factum est verbum Domini, angelo mediante, et intus loquente, ad Zachariam filium Barachiæ, filium Addo, prophetam.
paras.en: As St. Jerome says, among the twelve Prophets the most obscure is Zacharias, whose book is now, with God's light, to be explained. In his prologue this Prophet has made known at what time he began to prophesy. [[1:1|In the eighth month, in the second year|In mense octavo, in anno secundo]], that is, in the eighth month of the second year of the reign [[1:1|of king Darius|Darii regis]] of the Persians, of whom we have already spoken at the beginning of the exposition of the prophet Aggeus[[Agg 1:1||]]; [[1:1|the word of the Lord came|factum est verbum Domini]], through an angel as mediator, speaking within, [[1:1|to Zechariah the son of Barachias, the son of Addo, the prophet|ad Zachariam filium Barachiæ, filium Addo, prophetam]] [a marginal note gives the variant *filii* for the second *filium*: "son of Barachias, son of Addo" would then make Barachias the son of Addo, as the Vulgate reads; Denis's argument below follows *filium*, which makes Zacharias himself "son of Addo"].

paras.t: Erantque Barachias et Addo Prophetæ, secundum dictum Hebræorum, asserentium illos omnes fuisse Prophetas, qui in titulo Prophetarum exprimuntur. Hieronymus quoque affirmat, hunc Addo fuisse Prophetam quem misit Deus ad Jeroboam stantem super altare et thus idolo jacientem, prout tertio Regum libro legitur. Quod si verum est, constat quod Addo iste non fuit proximus pater Barachiæ istius, nec avus Zachariæ, sed pater ejus remotus, sicut et Christus dicitur filius David. Siquidem Addo ille fuit in diebus Jeroboam regis Israel, qui annis centenis Babylonicam captivitatem præcessit. Verum, ut alii asserunt, dictum istud Hieronymi, de Scripturis auctoritatem non habet. Videtur tamen Hieronymus ex libro Paralipomenon assertionis hujus occasionem sumpsisse. Etenim secundo Paralipomenon libro scribitur : Opera Roboam prima et novissima scripta sunt in libro Semeiæ prophetæ et Addo videntis. Sed ibi non fertur quod Addo fuerit ad Jeroboam missus. Quod quamvis ibi vel alibi scriberetur, consequens tamen non esset quod fuisset iste Addo, quum diversi Prophetæ eisdem frequenter nominibus vocati noscantur. Nec est consuetudo Scripturæ, genealogiam Prophetarum per patrem et progenitorem ita remotum, intermediis patribus omissis, describere. Nihilo minus verbis Hieronymi apparentiam facit, quod in aliorum titulis Prophetarum, dum proximi progenitores narrantur, pater dicitur filius avi, et avus proavi, ita quod in eodem casu scribuntur, sicut in principio Sophoniæ prophetæ quo legitur : Verbum quod factum est ad Sophoniam filium Chusi, filii Godoliæ, filii Amariæ, filii Ezechiæ. Sed in titulo Zachariæ ita non agitur, quoniam Barachias qui scribitur pater Zachariæ, non dicitur filius Addo; sed dicitur : Factum est verbum Domini ad Zachariam filium Barachiæ, filium Addo. Sicque verisimiliter dici potest, quod ob commendationem sanctitatis et gratiæ suæ, præfatus Addo pater hujus Zachariæ vocetur, ceteris intermediis, qui gratiam prophetalem sortiti non sunt, non expressis.
paras.en: Now Barachias and Addo were Prophets, according to the saying of the Hebrews, who assert that all those named in the titles of the Prophets were Prophets. Jerome also affirms that this Addo was the Prophet whom God sent to Jeroboam as he stood upon the altar and burned incense to an idol, as we read in the third book of Kings[[3 Kings 13:1||]] [the margin gives II Reg. xiii, 1; the passage is 3 Kings 13:1, where the man of God is not named]. If that is true, it is clear that this Addo was not the immediate father of this Barachias, nor the grandfather of Zacharias, but his remote forefather, as Christ too is called the son of David. For that Addo lived in the days of Jeroboam king of Israel, who came hundreds of years before the Babylonian captivity. But, as others assert, this saying of Jerome has no authority from the Scriptures. Yet Jerome seems to have taken the occasion of this assertion from the book of Paralipomenon. For in the second book of Paralipomenon it is written: [[2 Par 12:15|the acts of Roboam first and last are written in the books of Semeias the prophet, and of Addo the seer|Opera Roboam prima et novissima scripta sunt in libro Semeiæ prophetæ et Addo videntis]]. But it is not said there that Addo was sent to Jeroboam. And even if this were written there or elsewhere, it still would not follow that it was this Addo, since different Prophets are known often to have been called by the same names. Nor is it the custom of Scripture to describe the genealogy of the Prophets through a father and a forefather so remote, leaving out the fathers between. Nevertheless, this lends some likelihood to Jerome's words: in the titles of other Prophets, when the nearest forefathers are given, the father is called the son of the grandfather, and the grandfather the son of the great-grandfather, so that they are written in the same case [that is, each in the genitive, "son of … son of …"], as at the beginning of the prophet Sophonias, where we read: [[Soph 1:1|The word of the Lord that came to Zephaniah the son of Chusi, the son of Godolias, the son of Amarias, the son of Ezechias|Verbum quod factum est ad Sophoniam filium Chusi, filii Godoliæ, filii Amariæ, filii Ezechiæ]]. But in the title of Zacharias it is not so, since Barachias, who is written as the father of Zacharias, is not called the son of Addo; rather it says: [[1:1|the word of the Lord came to Zechariah the son of Barachias, the son of Addo|Factum est verbum Domini ad Zachariam filium Barachiæ, filium Addo]]. And so it may be said with likelihood that, to commend his holiness and grace, the aforesaid Addo is called the father of this Zacharias, the others in between, who did not receive the grace of prophecy, being left unnamed.

paras.t: Porro Zacharias duobus post Aggæum mensibus orsus est prophetare, quemadmodum ex eorum proœmiis innotescit. Unde et Aggæus in ordine duodecim Prophetarum huic præponitur. Deinceps pariter prophetaverunt ad Judæos de Babylone reversos, juxta illud primi Esdræ : Prophetaverunt autem Aggæus propheta et Zacharias filius Addo ad Judæos, qui erant in Jerusalem, etc.
paras.en: Further, Zacharias began to prophesy two months after Aggeus, as is known from their prologues. Hence Aggeus is also placed before him in the order of the twelve Prophets. From then on they prophesied together to the Jews who had returned from Babylon, according to that of the first book of Esdras: [[1 Esd 5:1|Now Aggeus the prophet, and Zacharias the son of Addo, prophesied to the Jews that were in Judea and Jerusalem|Prophetaverunt autem Aggæus propheta et Zacharias filius Addo ad Judæos, qui erant in Jerusalem]], etc.

paras.t: Itaque, Factum est verbum Domini ad Zachariam, dicens per eum ad populum, vel ad eum sub persona populi : Iratus est Dominus (in quem nec mutatio, nec perturbatio, nec passio cadit : propter quod irasci non dicitur secundum passionis affectum, sed operis parilitatem, justitiæque rigorem, prout in Jeremia ait : Numquid me ad iracundiam provocant? dicit Dominus; nonne semetipsos in confusione vultus sui?) super patres vestros : quos tradidit in manibus Chaldæorum, a quibus gravissime oppressi fuerunt, juxta illud Jeremiæ : Nabuchodonosor rex Babylonis exossavit eos; iracundia, id est justa et rigorosa punitione qua eos punivit.
paras.en: So then, [[1:1|the word of the Lord came to Zechariah|Factum est verbum Domini ad Zachariam]], [[1:1|saying|dicens]] through him to the people, or to him in the person of the people: [[1:2|The Lord hath been exceeding angry|Iratus est Dominus]] (in whom there falls neither change, nor disturbance, nor passion; for which reason he is said to be angry not by a feeling of passion, but by the likeness of the work [that is, what God does is like what an angry man does, though there is no passion in him] and the rigour of justice, as he says in Jeremias: [[Jer 7:19|Do they provoke me to anger, saith the Lord? is it not themselves, to the confusion of their own countenance|Numquid me ad iracundiam provocant? dicit Dominus; nonne semetipsos in confusione vultus sui]]?) [[1:2|with your fathers|super patres vestros]]: whom he delivered into the hands of the Chaldeans, by whom they were most grievously oppressed, according to that of Jeremias: [[Jer 50:17|Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon hath broken his bones|Nabuchodonosor rex Babylonis exossavit eos]] [the margin gives Ibid. i, 17; the words are at Jer 50:17]; [[1:2|exceeding|iracundia]] [Latin *iracundia*, "with anger", which the Douay-Rheims renders by "exceeding"], that is, with the just and rigorous punishment with which he punished them.

paras.t: Et dices tu, Zacharia, ad eos : Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum : Convertimini ad me, corda vestra ad gratiam disponendo, actibusque pœnitentiæ insistendo, ait Dominus exercituum; et convertar ad vos, peccata delendo, et gratiam infundendo, augendo et conservando, dicit Dominus exercituum, id est agminum supernorum seu angelicorum spirituum. In Hebræo habetur, Dominus Sabaoth : pro quo Septuaginta interpretes aliquando, Deus seu Dominus omnipotens, aliquando, Dominus virtutum, transtulerunt. Denique, secundum Hieronymum, Aggæus et Zacharias in paucis versiculis brevibusque sententiis semper adjiciunt, Dicit Dominus exercituum, ut hi quibus loquebantur, scirent Dominum esse qui præcipit, ac per hoc adversus regis imperium circumfrementesque hostes ad templi ædificationem fiducialiter concitarentur. Hoc tamen de Dario rege accipiendum non puto, quum juxta præhabita dederit copiosam ad templi reparationem licentiam, sed forte de Artaxerxe.
paras.en: [[1:3|And thou shalt say|Et dices]], thou, Zacharias, [[1:3|to them: Thus saith the Lord of hosts: Turn ye to me|ad eos : Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum : Convertimini ad me]], by disposing your hearts for grace and applying yourselves to works of penance, [[1:3|saith the Lord of hosts: and I will turn to you|ait Dominus exercituum; et convertar ad vos]], by blotting out sins, and by pouring in grace, increasing and preserving it, [[1:3|saith the Lord of hosts|dicit Dominus exercituum]], that is, of the heavenly hosts or of the angelic spirits. In the Hebrew it is *Lord Sabaoth*: for which the Seventy translators put sometimes *God* or *Lord almighty*, sometimes *Lord of powers*. Moreover, according to Jerome, Aggeus and Zacharias, every few short verses and brief sentences, always add *Saith the Lord of hosts*, so that those to whom they spoke might know that it was the Lord who commanded, and so might be stirred up to build the temple with confidence against the king's command and the enemies raging round about. Yet I do not think this is to be taken of king Darius, since, as was said before, he gave ample licence to repair the temple[[1 Esd 6:1||]][[1 Esd 6:14||]], but perhaps of Artaxerxes.

paras.t: Quæritur, quum nemo queat converti ad Deum, nisi Deus primo per gratiæ infusionem convertatur ad ipsum (juxta illud Jeremiæ in Threnis seu Lamentationibus : Converte nos, Domine, ad te, et convertemur. Unde et rursus Jeremias inducit : Converte me, Domine, et convertar : postquam enim convertisti me, egi pœnitentiam), quomodo nunc loquitur Dominus, Convertimini ad me, et convertar ad vos. Et respondendum, quod Dominus non præcipit hoc de conversione virtuosa ac meritoria per caritatem et gratiam, sed de conversione inchoativa, qua quis ad Dei gratiam se ipsum habilitat, faciendo quod in se est. Juxta quod scriptum est : Appropinquate Deo, et appropinquabit vobis; et in Psalmo, Accedite ad eum, et illuminamini. Paulus quoque : Surge, inquit, qui dormis, et illuminabit te Christus. Si vero verbum illud dirigatur ad eos qui jam sunt in gratia Dei, intelligendum est de spirituali profectu et actuali tendentia mentis in Deum : quod tamen non fit sine prævia motione Spiritus Sancti.
paras.en: It is asked: since no one can be turned to God unless God first turns to him by the infusion of grace (according to that of Jeremias in the Threnody or Lamentations: [[Lam 5:21|Convert us, O Lord, to thee, and we shall be converted|Converte nos, Domine, ad te, et convertemur]]. Hence Jeremias again brings in: [[Jer 31:18|Convert me, and I shall be converted|Converte me, Domine, et convertar]]: [[Jer 31:19|For after thou didst convert me, I did penance|postquam enim convertisti me, egi pœnitentiam]]), how does the Lord now say, [[1:3|Turn ye to me|Convertimini ad me]], and [[1:3|I will turn to you|convertar ad vos]]? The answer is that the Lord does not command this of the virtuous and meritorious conversion through charity and grace, but of the inchoate conversion [that is, the first beginning of turning to God, before grace is given], by which one makes oneself fit for the grace of God by doing what lies in him [the schoolmen's maxim: to one who does what lies in him, God does not deny grace]. According to what is written: [[Jas 4:8|Draw nigh to God: and he will draw nigh to you|Appropinquate Deo, et appropinquabit vobis]]; and in the Psalm, [[Ps 33:6|Come ye to him and be enlightened|Accedite ad eum, et illuminamini]]. Paul too: [[Eph 5:14|Rise|Surge]], he says, [[Eph 5:14|thou that sleepest|qui dormis]], [[Eph 5:14|and Christ shall enlighten thee|et illuminabit te Christus]]. But if that word is addressed to those who are already in the grace of God, it is to be understood of spiritual progress and the actual tending of the mind toward God; which nevertheless does not happen without the prior motion of the Holy Ghost.

paras.t: Insuper, juxta mysticam rationem, per hoc quod Deus toties in Scripturis Dominum exercituum appellari se voluit, insinuatur quod pertinentes ad se vult esse armatos fortesque milites, et stare in acie contra adversarias potestates, ut virtutibus cunctis muniti, victorialiter dimicent contra mundum, carnem atque diabolum.
paras.en: Besides, according to the mystical sense, by God's having willed to be called so often in the Scriptures *the Lord of hosts*, it is intimated that he wills those who belong to him to be armed and brave soldiers, and to stand in battle array against the adverse powers, so that, fortified with all the virtues, they may fight victoriously against the world, the flesh and the devil.

paras.t: Ne sitis sicut patres vestri indurati et impœnitentes, ad quos clamabant magno caritatis fervore et voce sonora, sicut Isaias hortatur, Quasi tuba exalta vocem tuam, Prophetæ priores, qui ante me fuerunt, sive in Babylone, ut Daniel et Ezechiel, sive in Jerusalem et Judæa ante Babylonicam captivitatem, ut Jeremias, Sophonias, etc., dicentes : Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum : Convertimini ad Deum de viis, id est operibus atque affectibus, vestris malis, et cogitationibus vestris pessimis. Hoc omnes clamaverunt Prophetæ. Unde et per Isaiam Dominus ait : Auferte malum cogitationum vestrarum ab oculis meis. Et non audierunt auribus mentis : de quibus loquitur in Evangelio Christus, Qui habet aures audiendi, audiat; neque attenderunt ad me, verba mea considerando, divinam justitiam intuendo, divinis præceptis obtemperando; dicit Dominus.
paras.en: [[1:4|Be not as your fathers|Ne sitis sicut patres vestri]], hardened and impenitent, to whom [[1:4|have cried|ad quos clamabant]], with great fervour of charity and a ringing voice, as Isaias exhorts, [[Is 58:1|lift up thy voice like a trumpet|Quasi tuba exalta vocem tuam]], [[1:4|the former prophets|Prophetæ priores]], who were before me, whether in Babylon, as Daniel and Ezechiel, or in Jerusalem and Judea before the Babylonian captivity, as Jeremias, Sophonias, etc., [[1:4|saying: Thus saith the Lord of hosts: Turn ye|dicentes : Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum : Convertimini]] to God [[1:4|from your evil ways|de viis]], that is, works and affections, [[1:4|and from your wicked thoughts|vestris malis, et cogitationibus vestris pessimis]]. All the Prophets cried out this. Hence the Lord says through Isaias too: [[Is 1:16|take away the evil of your devices from my eyes|Auferte malum cogitationum vestrarum ab oculis meis]]. [[1:4|But they did not give ear|Et non audierunt]] with the ears of the mind, of which Christ speaks in the Gospel, [[Luke 8:8|He that hath ears to hear, let him hear|Qui habet aures audiendi, audiat]]; [[1:4|neither did they hearken to me|neque attenderunt ad me]], by considering my words, beholding the divine justice, obeying the divine commands; [[1:4|saith the Lord|dicit Dominus]].

paras.t: Patres vestri, qui non attenderunt ad me, ubi sunt? quasi dicat : In suis vanitatibus defecerunt, et de hac temporali, brevi ac labili vita, ad æternam damnationem perducti sunt. Et prophetæ eorum fallaces? Loquitur enim de falsis, nam subditur : Numquid in sempiternum vivent? quasi diceret : Nequaquam; imo æternam mortem illapsi sunt. Quocontra scriptum est : Justi in perpetuum vivent; et rursus, Et si coram hominibus tormenta passi sunt, spes electorum immortalitate plena est. De his falsis prophetis multa loquitur Jeremias : Mendacium, inquiens, et seductionem cordis sui loquuntur vobis; et denuo, Propheta namque et sacerdos abierunt in viam quam ignoraverunt. Loquitur itaque nunc Dominus de prophetis iniquis, qui Judæis promiserunt Jerusalem capiendam non esse a Chaldæis : qui simul cum aliis perierunt.
paras.en: [[1:5|Your fathers|Patres vestri]], who did not hearken to me, [[1:5|where are they|ubi sunt]]? as if to say: They have failed in their vanities, and from this temporal, short and slippery life have been led away to eternal damnation. [[1:5|and the prophets|Et prophetæ]], their deceivers? [Denis reads *prophetæ eorum fallaces*, "their lying prophets"] For he speaks of the false ones, since it follows: [[1:5|shall they live always|Numquid in sempiternum vivent]]? as if he said: By no means; rather they have fallen into eternal death. Against which it is written: [[Wis 5:16|the just shall live for evermore|Justi in perpetuum vivent]]; and again, [[Wis 3:4|though in the sight of men they suffered torments, their hope is full of immortality|Et si coram hominibus tormenta passi sunt, spes electorum immortalitate plena est]] [Denis reads "the hope of the elect"]. Of these false prophets Jeremias says much: [[Jer 14:14|a lying vision|Mendacium]], he says, [[Jer 14:14|and the seduction of their own heart|et seductionem cordis sui]] [[Jer 14:14|they prophesy unto you|loquuntur vobis]]; and again, [[Jer 14:18|The prophet also and the priest are gone into a land which they knew not|Propheta namque et sacerdos abierunt in viam quam ignoraverunt]] [Denis reads *in viam*, "into a way", where the Vulgate has *in terram*, "into a land"]. So the Lord now speaks of the wicked prophets who promised the Jews that Jerusalem would not be taken by the Chaldeans: who perished together with the rest.

paras.t: Verumtamen verba mea, quibus patrum vestrorum captivitatem prædixi, et legitima mea, id est præcepta de illorum punitione, nisi se emendarent, quæ mandavi servis meis Prophetis ut proponerent ea ipsis, numquid non comprehenderunt patres vestros? id est, imo super eos venerunt, et in ipsis verificata consistunt. Hinc in persona istorum scriptum est in Daniele : Peccavimus, et inique egimus, recedentes a te, et præcepta tua non observavimus, et tradidisti nos in manibus iniquorum. Et conversi sunt : id est, quidam eorum considerando plagas sibi a Deo illatas, pœnituerunt, secundum illud Isaiæ : Tantummodo sola vexatio dabit intellectum auditui; itemque in Psalmo, Imple facies eorum ignominia, et quærent nomen tuum, Domine; et dixerunt : Sicut cogitavit Dominus exercituum facere nobis secundum vias nostras, et secundum adinventiones nostras, id est, quemadmodum decrevit atque prædixit reddere nobis secundum exigentiam iniquitatum nostrarum, sic fecit nobis, derelinquendo nos in captivitate Babylonica septuaginta annis.
paras.en: [[1:6|But yet my words|Verumtamen verba mea]], by which I foretold the captivity of your fathers, [[1:6|and my ordinances|et legitima mea]], that is, the commands about their punishment unless they amended, [[1:6|which I gave in charge to my servants the prophets|quæ mandavi servis meis Prophetis]] to set before them, [[1:6|did they not take hold of your fathers|numquid non comprehenderunt patres vestros]]? that is, they did indeed come upon them, and stand fulfilled in them. Hence it is written in Daniel in the person of these men: [[Dan 3:29|we have sinned, and committed iniquity, departing from thee|Peccavimus, et inique egimus, recedentes a te]], and have not kept thy commandments[[Dan 3:30||]], [[Dan 3:32|and thou hast delivered us into the hands|et tradidisti nos in manibus]] of the wicked. [[1:6|and they returned|Et conversi sunt]] [*conversi sunt*, "they were turned", that is, converted]: that is, some of them, considering the strokes brought upon them by God, repented, according to that of Isaias: [[Is 28:19|vexation alone shall make you understand what you hear|Tantummodo sola vexatio dabit intellectum auditui]]; and likewise in the Psalm, [[Ps 82:17|Fill their faces with shame; and they shall seek thy name, O Lord|Imple facies eorum ignominia, et quærent nomen tuum, Domine]]; [[1:6|and said: As the Lord of hosts thought to do to us according to our ways, and according to our devices|et dixerunt : Sicut cogitavit Dominus exercituum facere nobis secundum vias nostras, et secundum adinventiones nostras]], that is, as he decreed and foretold that he would repay us according to the measure of our iniquities, [[1:6|so he hath done to us|sic fecit nobis]], leaving us in the Babylonian captivity for seventy years.

paras.t: Consequenter consolatur Propheta populum Judæorum, a captivitate reversum. In die vicesima et quarta undecimi mensis nomine Sabath, secundum linguam Hebræam, in anno secundo Darii, utpote tertio mense post primam visionem, quæ facta est mense octavo anni secundi Darii regis, factum est verbum Domini ad Zachariam filium Barachiæ, filium Addo, prophetam, dicens, id est, ad loquendum inducens ac instruens Zachariam : qui ex verbo Dei in anima sua angelica revelatione formato, motus est ad dicendum quæ subsequuntur.
paras.en: Next the Prophet comforts the people of the Jews returned from captivity. [[1:7|In the four and twentieth day of the eleventh month|In die vicesima et quarta undecimi mensis]], [[1:7|which is called Sabath|nomine Sabath]] in the Hebrew tongue, [[1:7|in the second year of Darius|in anno secundo Darii]], that is, in the third month after the first vision, which took place in the eighth month of the second year of king Darius, [[1:7|the word of the Lord came to Zechariah the son of Barachias, the son of Addo, the prophet, saying|factum est verbum Domini ad Zachariam filium Barachiæ, filium Addo, prophetam, dicens]], that is, moving and instructing Zacharias to speak: who, by the word of God formed in his soul through the revelation of an angel, was moved to say what follows.

paras.t: Vidi per noctem, id est tempore nocturno, quod divinis revelationibus suscipiendis propter silentium sensuumque et phantasiæ quietem aptius fertur. Propter quod in libro Job scribitur : Per somnium in visione nocturna, quando sopor irruit super homines, aperit Deus aures virorum. Unde visio ista imaginaria fuit, et forte in somno. Et ecce apparuit mihi in visione hac vir ascendens super equum rufum. Per virum intelligitur angelus Dei in forma viri apparens, secundum quod Daniel ait : Vir Gabriel stetit coram me. Et in Actuum libro de angelis legitur : Ecce duo viri adstiterunt juxta illos. Porro per equum rufum, propter rubeum colorem, significata est ultio Dei, adversariis Judæorum infligenda, propter peccata in Judæos commissa. Et ut refert Hieronymus, per angelum istum Hebræi intelligunt Michaelem, qui ultor fuit iniquitatum in Judæos factarum, et præfuit Synagogæ.
paras.en: [[1:8|I saw by night|Vidi per noctem]], that is, at night-time, which is said to be more fit for receiving divine revelations, because of the silence and the quiet of the senses and of the imagination. For this reason it is written in the book of Job: [[Job 33:15|By a dream in a vision by night, when deep sleep falleth upon men|Per somnium in visione nocturna, quando sopor irruit super homines]], [[Job 33:16|he openeth the ears of men|aperit Deus aures virorum]]. Hence this vision was imaginary [that is, seen in images formed in the imagination, not with the bodily eyes nor by the understanding alone], and perhaps in sleep. [[1:8|and behold|Et ecce]] there appeared to me in this vision [[1:8|a man riding upon a red horse|vir ascendens super equum rufum]]. By the man is understood an angel of God appearing in the form of a man, as Daniel says: [[Dan 9:21|the man, Gabriel|Vir Gabriel]] stood before me[[Dan 8:15||]]. And in the book of Acts we read of angels: [[Acts 1:10|behold two men stood by them|Ecce duo viri adstiterunt juxta illos]]. Further, by the red horse, because of its red colour, is signified the vengeance of God that was to be inflicted on the enemies of the Jews for the sins committed against the Jews. And, as Jerome relates, by this angel the Hebrews understand Michael, who was the avenger of the wrongs done to the Jews, and was set over the Synagogue.

paras.t: Et ipse stabat inter myrteta, id est in locis ubi crescunt myrti, qui sunt arbores elegantes, poma odorifera atque pulcherrima proferentes : propter quod dicit Hieronymus, quod per myrtum significabatur lætitia Judæis adfutura de templi et terræ recuperatione. Judæi quoque secundum Hieronymum, per myrtos intelligunt Prophetas et sanctos, qui in medio populi Judæorum in Chaldæa captivorum versabantur, inter quos sanctos angelus libenter tunc stetit. Quæ erant in profundo : quia in convalle nascuntur, vel apparebant, et quoniam Prophetæ et sancti in profundo humilitatis atque in alto contemplationis exstiterant. Unde Septuaginta transtulerunt : Ipse stabat inter montes umbrosos.
paras.en: [[1:8|and he stood among the myrtle trees|Et ipse stabat inter myrteta]], that is, in places where myrtles grow, which are graceful trees bearing fragrant and very beautiful fruit; for which reason Jerome says that the myrtle signified the joy that would come to the Jews from the recovery of the temple and the land. The Jews too, according to Jerome, understand by the myrtles the Prophets and saints who lived in the midst of the people of the Jews held captive in Chaldea, among which saints the angel then gladly stood. [[1:8|that were in the bottom|Quæ erant in profundo]]: because they grow in a valley, or appeared there; and because the Prophets and saints stood in the depth of humility and on the height of contemplation. Hence the Seventy translated: He stood among the shady mountains.

paras.t: Et post eum equi rufi, varii, et albi. Per equos rufos, propter rubeum colorem intelliguntur illi qui populum Judæorum graviter afflixerunt, eorumque sanguinem effuderunt, puta Chaldæi, vel (ut Judæi exponunt) Romani. Per equos albos intelliguntur, qui Judæis clementes fuerunt, videlicet Persæ et Medi, quorum reges remiserunt Judæos de Chaldæa in propriam terram, et licentiam reædificandi Jerusalem templumque in ea, largiti sunt, scilicet Cyrus ac Darius. Per varios equos intelliguntur Græci sive Macedones, quorum quidam fuerunt Judæis amici, alii persecutores, ut patet in libro Machabæorum, et in ultima visione Danielis prophetæ. Quidam nomine equorum dicunt etiam ascensores equorum insinuari, atque per ascensores equorum intelligunt angelos præfatis regnis prælatos. Quidam autem per equos intelligunt angelos, divini imperii promptissimos atque fortissimos exsecutores, qui propter ordinum distinctionem albi, rufi, variique dicuntur.
paras.en: [[1:8|and behind him were horses, red, speckled, and white|Et post eum equi rufi, varii, et albi]]. By the red horses, because of the red colour, are understood those who grievously afflicted the people of the Jews and shed their blood, for instance the Chaldeans, or (as the Jews explain it) the Romans. By the white horses are understood those who were merciful to the Jews, namely the Persians and Medes, whose kings sent the Jews back from Chaldea to their own land and granted them licence to rebuild Jerusalem and the temple in it, that is, Cyrus and Darius[[1 Esd 1:1||]][[1 Esd 6:1||]]. By the speckled horses are understood the Greeks or Macedonians, some of whom were friends to the Jews, others persecutors, as is plain in the book of Machabees[[1 Mach 1:1||]] [the margin gives 1 Mach. passim] and in the last vision of the prophet Daniel[[Dan 11:1||]]. Some say that by the name of horses their riders too are meant, and by the riders of the horses they understand the angels set over the aforesaid kingdoms. Others again understand by the horses angels, the most ready and most mighty executors of the divine command, who are called white, red and speckled because of the distinction of their orders.

paras.t: Et dixi ego Zacharias, ad angelum per quem fiebant mihi revelationes propheticæ : Quid sunt isti? id est, quid equi isti designant, Domine mi angele Dei? Dicuntque aliqui, quod iste fuit angelus Zachariæ ad custodiam deputatus : quod certum non reor, quum constet propheticas revelationes non semper exhibitas per angelos Prophetarum custodiis deputatos. Unde Gabriel qui Danieli loquebatur, legitur in Evangelio Zachariæ sacerdoti et Virgini benedictæ futura prædicere. Et dixit ad me angelus qui loquebatur in me, cujus ministerio Deus mihi futura ostendit : ita quod angelus iste formavit in spiritu et imaginativa virtute Zachariæ formas, phantasmata, sive imagines rerum quæ sibi præmonstrabantur, deditque ei intelligere quid imagines istæ significarent. Intelligentia enim est opus in visione. Ideo subditur : Ego ostendam tibi, per me ipsum vel angelum superiorem, quid sint hæc, id est, quid equi isti significent.
paras.en: [[1:9|And I said|Et dixi]], I Zacharias, to the angel through whom the prophetic revelations came to me: [[1:9|What are these|Quid sunt isti]]? that is, what do these horses signify, [[1:9|my Lord|Domine mi]], angel of God? Some say that this was the angel appointed to guard Zacharias: which I do not think certain, since it is clear that prophetic revelations were not always shown through the angels appointed to guard the Prophets. Hence Gabriel, who spoke to Daniel[[Dan 9:21||]], is read in the Gospel to have foretold things to come to Zachary the priest[[Luke 1:11||]] and to the blessed Virgin[[Luke 1:26||]]. [[1:9|and the angel that spoke in me, said to me|Et dixit ad me angelus qui loquebatur in me]], by whose ministry God showed me things to come; so that this angel formed in the spirit and imaginative power of Zacharias the forms, phantasms or images of the things that were being shown him, and gave him to understand what those images signified. [[Dan 10:1|for there is need of understanding in a vision|Intelligentia enim est opus in visione]]. Therefore it follows: [[1:9|I will shew thee|Ego ostendam tibi]], by myself or by a higher angel, [[1:9|what these are|quid sint hæc]], that is, what these horses signify.

paras.t: Et respondit vir qui stabat inter myrteta, et dixit : id est, angelo qui in me loquebatur, per se ipsum non respondente, sed paulisper tacente, angelus stans inter myrteta, angelo in me loquente id impetrante, mihi respondit : Isti sunt, quos misit Dominus ut perambulent terram : id est, equi præscripti significant populos memoratos seu regna præfata, quæ nutu divino diversas regiones peragraverunt, easque suo dominio subjecerunt. Vel, Isti sunt, etc., id est, angelos divinæ voluntatis exsecutores, et terram celeriter perambulantes, significant.
paras.en: [[1:10|And the man that stood among the myrtle trees answered, and said|Et respondit vir qui stabat inter myrteta, et dixit]]: that is, while the angel who spoke in me did not answer by himself but kept silent for a little, the angel standing among the myrtle trees, at the request of the angel speaking in me, answered me: [[1:10|These are they, whom the Lord hath sent to walk through the earth|Isti sunt, quos misit Dominus ut perambulent terram]]: that is, the horses described signify the peoples mentioned, or the aforesaid kingdoms, which by God's will went through various regions and brought them under their dominion. Or, [[1:10|These are they|Isti sunt]], etc., that is, they signify the angels, executors of the divine will, who walk swiftly through the earth.

paras.t: Et responderunt angeli regnis ac nationibus præsidentes, angelo Domini, qui stabat inter myrteta, id est superiori angelo qui præfuit Synagogæ, et erat de ordine Principatuum, scilicet Michael princeps magnus, qui stetit pro filiis Israel, ut dicit Daniel. Et dixerunt : Perambulavimus terram, id est, statum regnorum pensavimus, et per diversa loca processimus, nobis commissos custodiendo. Nec oportet perambulationem istam humano more intelligi, quanquam angeli interdum more hominum cum hominibus ambulasse legantur, ut Raphael cum Tobia, et angeli cum Abraham et Lot. Et ecce omnis terra habitatur, et quiescit, id est, omnia regna sub nostra custodia tuta sunt atque pacata, nec prælia notabilia jam exsurgunt.
paras.en: [[1:11|And they answered|Et responderunt]], the angels presiding over kingdoms and nations, [[1:11|the angel of the Lord, that stood among the myrtle trees|angelo Domini, qui stabat inter myrteta]], that is, the higher angel who was set over the Synagogue and was of the order of Principalities, namely Michael, [[Dan 12:1|the great prince, who standeth for the children|princeps magnus, qui stetit pro filiis]] of Israel, as Daniel says. [[1:11|and said: We have walked through the earth|Et dixerunt : Perambulavimus terram]], that is, we have weighed the state of the kingdoms and gone forth through various places, guarding those committed to us. Nor need this walking through be understood in a human way, although angels are sometimes read to have walked with men in the manner of men, as Raphael with Tobias[[Tob 5:21||]][[Tob 12:15||]], and the angels with Abraham[[Gen 18:16||]] and Lot[[Gen 19:16||]][[Gen 19:17||]]. [[1:11|and behold all the earth is inhabited, and is at rest|Et ecce omnis terra habitatur, et quiescit]], that is, all the kingdoms in our keeping are safe and at peace, and no notable wars now arise.

paras.t: Et respondit angelus Domini, et dixit, ille qui stetit inter myrteta, interpellans pro Judæis, et ex verbis angelorum prædictorum occasionem accipiens orandi pro eis, utpote præsidens Synagogæ. Hic ergo respondit, id est, ad præinducta verba convenienter locutus est : Domine exercituum, usquequo tu non misereberis Jerusalem et urbium Juda, quibus iratus es? id est, quum cetera regna idololatriæ dedita prosperentur, quamdiu differes reædificationem Jerusalem et urbium regni Juda, quorum peccata hucusque castigasti, et oppida reliquisti destructa? Iste jam septuagesimus annus est : id est, septuaginta anni fluxerunt, quibus evolutis, dixisti te miseraturum urbibus istis et populo Judæorum per Jeremiam prophetam, juxta illud : Quum cœperint impleri in Babylone septuaginta anni, visitabo vos et suscitabo super vos verbum meum bonum.
paras.en: [[1:12|And the angel of the Lord answered, and said|Et respondit angelus Domini, et dixit]], he who stood among the myrtle trees, interceding for the Jews and, from the words of the angels aforesaid, taking occasion to pray for them, as the one presiding over the Synagogue. He then answered, that is, spoke fittingly to the words just brought in: [[1:12|O Lord of hosts, how long wilt thou not have mercy on Jerusalem, and on the cities of Juda, with which thou hast been angry|Domine exercituum, usquequo tu non misereberis Jerusalem et urbium Juda, quibus iratus es]]? that is, while the other kingdoms given to idolatry prosper, how long wilt thou put off the rebuilding of Jerusalem and of the cities of the kingdom of Juda, whose sins thou hast chastised until now, and whose towns thou hast left destroyed? [[1:12|this is now the seventieth year|Iste jam septuagesimus annus est]]: that is, seventy years have passed, at the end of which thou didst say through the prophet Jeremias that thou wouldst have mercy on these cities and on the people of the Jews, according to that: [[Jer 29:10|When the seventy years shall begin to be accomplished in Babylon, I will visit you: and I will perform my good word in your favour|Quum cœperint impleri in Babylone septuaginta anni, visitabo vos et suscitabo super vos verbum meum bonum]].

paras.t: Sed quum anni isti fuerint tempore Cyri regis impleti, quando relaxavit captivitatem Judæorum in Babylone, qualiter Zacharias ait, quod tempore hujus prophetiæ, videlicet secundo anno Darii, septuagesimus fuerit annus, præsertim quum (teste Hieronymo) inter primum annum Cyri et annum secundum Darii fluxerint anni quadraginta? Et respondendum, quod numerus major non excludit minorem.
paras.en: But since these years were fulfilled in the time of king Cyrus, when he released the captivity of the Jews in Babylon[[1 Esd 1:1||]][[1 Esd 1:3||]], how does Zacharias say that at the time of this prophecy, namely in the second year of Darius, it was the seventieth year, especially since (as Jerome witnesses) forty years passed between the first year of Cyrus and the second year of Darius? The answer is that the greater number does not exclude the smaller [that is, the seventy years have been reached, though more have in fact gone by].

paras.t: Et respondit Dominus angelo qui loquebatur in me, verba bona, verba consolatoria, scilicet quod Jerusalem, urbesque Juda repararentur, et populus Judæorum prosperaretur.
paras.en: [[1:13|And the Lord answered the angel, that spoke in me, good words, comfortable words|Et respondit Dominus angelo qui loquebatur in me, verba bona, verba consolatoria]], namely, that Jerusalem and the cities of Juda would be restored, and the people of the Jews would prosper.

paras.t: Et dixit ad me angelus qui loquebatur in me : Clama ad Judæos, dicens : Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum : Zelatus sum Jerusalem et Sion zelo magno, id est, magno ac speciali amore dilexi populum Judæorum et quæ pertinebant ad eos, atque ex isto amore tam diligenter et aspere correxi ejus excessus, ut in posterum cautior sit, quemadmodum vir uxorem carissimam, si infidelis sibi fuerit, asperrime corripit. Hoc quantum ad electos verificatur; quantum vero ad reprobos populi hujus, Dominus ait per Ezechielem : Zelus meus recessit a te.
paras.en: [[1:14|And the angel that spoke in me, said to me: Cry thou|Et dixit ad me angelus qui loquebatur in me : Clama]] to the Jews, [[1:14|saying: Thus saith the Lord of hosts: I am zealous for Jerusalem, and Sion with a great zeal|dicens : Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum : Zelatus sum Jerusalem et Sion zelo magno]], that is, I have loved with a great and special love the people of the Jews and what belonged to them, and out of that love I have corrected its excesses so carefully and so sharply that it may be more cautious hereafter, as a man most sharply rebukes a dearly loved wife if she has been unfaithful to him. This holds true as regards the elect; but as regards the reprobate of this people, the Lord says through Ezechiel: [[Ezech 16:42|my jealousy shall depart from thee|Zelus meus recessit a te]] [*zelus*, the "zeal" of this verse; Denis reads *recessit*, "has departed"].

paras.t: Et ira magna ego irascor super gentes opulentas, id est regnis et gentibus quæ Judæorum populum afflixerunt. His iratus est Dominus ira magna, quia non tantum in sæculo isto, sed et æternaliter eos perire præcepit. Unde secundo Machabæorum libro habetur : Non enim, sicut in aliis nationibus Deus patienter exspectat, ut eas, quum judicii dies advenerit, in plenitudine peccatorum puniat; ita et in nobis statuit, ut peccatis nostris in finem devolutis, ita demum in nos vindicet : propter quod nunquam a nobis misericordiam suam amovet; corripiens vero in adversis, populum suum non derelinquit.
paras.en: [[1:15|And I am angry with a great anger with the wealthy nations|Et ira magna ego irascor super gentes opulentas]], that is, with the kingdoms and nations that afflicted the people of the Jews. With these the Lord is angry with a great anger, because he has decreed that they perish not only in this world but eternally. Hence it is said in the second book of Machabees: [[2 Mach 6:14|For, not as with other nations, whom the Lord patiently expecteth, that when the day of judgment shall come, he may punish them in the fulness of their sins|Non enim, sicut in aliis nationibus Deus patienter exspectat, ut eas, quum judicii dies advenerit, in plenitudine peccatorum puniat]]; [[2 Mach 6:15|doth he also deal with us, so as to suffer our sins to come to their height, and then take vengeance on us|ita et in nobis statuit, ut peccatis nostris in finem devolutis, ita demum in nos vindicet]]: [[2 Mach 6:16|And therefore he never withdraweth his mercy from us: but though he chastise his people with adversity he forsaketh them not|propter quod nunquam a nobis misericordiam suam amovet; corripiens vero in adversis, populum suum non derelinquit]].

paras.t: Quia ego iratus sum parum, id est, vos Judæos citra condignum punivi, et pro damnatione æterna quam meruistis, temporali pœna vos castigavi intentione emendandi, non conterendi ; ipsi vero adjuverunt, id est, exsecutioni justitiæ meæ cooperati sunt circa vos, in malum, id est crudeliter atque perversa intentione. Quamvis enim Assyrii et Chaldæi, Deo ordinante, Judaicam plebem vastaverint, in quantum Deus per illos voluit populi sui peccata in præsenti punire; ipsi tamen intuitu Dei et zelo justitiæ id non fecerunt, sed ex superbia, cupiditate, et pessimo fine. Hinc per Isaiam Dominus ait : Væ Assur, virga furoris mei et baculus ipse est; ipse autem non sic arbitrabitur, sed ad conterendum erit cor ejus, et ad perdendas gentes.
paras.en: [[1:15|for I was angry a little|Quia ego iratus sum parum]], that is, I punished you Jews less than you deserved, and instead of the eternal damnation you merited I chastised you with a temporal penalty, meaning to amend you, not to crush you; [[1:15|but they helped forward|ipsi vero adjuverunt]], that is, they co-operated in the execution of my justice upon you, [[1:15|the evil|in malum]], that is, cruelly and with a perverse intention. For although the Assyrians and Chaldeans, by God's ordering, laid waste the Jewish people[[4 Kings 17:1||]][[4 Kings 25:1||]], inasmuch as God willed through them to punish the sins of his people in the present, yet they did not do it with an eye to God and out of zeal for justice, but from pride, greed and the worst of ends. Hence the Lord says through Isaias: [[Is 10:5|Woe to the Assyrian, he is the rod and the staff of my anger|Væ Assur, virga furoris mei et baculus ipse est]]; [[Is 10:7|But he shall not take it so|ipse autem non sic arbitrabitur]], [[Is 10:7|but his heart shall be set to destroy, and to cut off nations|sed ad conterendum erit cor ejus, et ad perdendas gentes]].

paras.t: Propterea hæc dicit Dominus, qui quum iratus fuerit, misericordiæ recordatur : Revertar, non locum mutando, qui incircumscriptus illocalisque sum, ad Jerusalem in misericordiis, id est ad populum Juda et urbem per varios pietatis meæ effectus multipliciter eis benefaciendo; et domus mea, id est templum, ædificabitur in ea, ait Dominus exercituum : quod sub Zorobabel factum est; et perpendiculum, id est hujusmodi instrumentum cæmentariorum, quo perpenditur an murus vel paries convenienter et recte ædificentur, extendetur super Jerusalem : quod factum est, quando muri et domus civitatis ædificabantur sub Esdra et Nehemia, sicut in libro Esdræ describitur.
paras.en: [[1:16|Therefore thus saith the Lord|Propterea hæc dicit Dominus]], who, when he is angry, remembers mercy[[Hab 3:2||]]: [[1:16|I will return|Revertar]], not by changing place, for I am uncircumscribed and not in a place, [[1:16|to Jerusalem in mercies|ad Jerusalem in misericordiis]], that is, to the people of Juda and the city, doing them good in many ways through the various effects of my loving-kindness; [[1:16|my house|et domus mea]], that is, the temple, [[1:16|shall be built in it, saith the Lord of hosts|ædificabitur in ea, ait Dominus exercituum]]: which was done under Zorobabel[[1 Esd 6:15||]] [the margin gives II Esdr. vi, 15, which tells of the finishing of the wall; the finishing of the temple is told at 1 Esd 6:15]; [[1:16|and the building line|et perpendiculum]] [*perpendiculum*, a plumb line], that is, the masons' instrument by which one tests whether a wall or partition is being built fittingly and straight, [[1:16|shall be stretched forth upon Jerusalem|extendetur super Jerusalem]]: which was done when the walls and houses of the city were being built under Esdras and Nehemias, as is described in the book of Esdras[[1 Esd 3:1||]][[1 Esd 6:1||]][[2 Esd 2:1||]] [the margin gives 1 Esdr. iii, vi; 2 Esdr. ii–iv].

paras.t: Insuper angelus præcipit Zachariæ : Adhuc clama, dicens : Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum : Adhuc affluent civitates meæ bonis : id est, post reditum de Babylone habitatores urbium Juda divitiis abundabunt, imo et spiritualibus gratiæ donis, quantum ad virtuosos : quod tempore Zorobabel, Esdræ et Prophetæ istius cœpit impleri; deinde post victoriam Judith et tempore Machabæorum, præsertim sub Simone sacerdote ac principe magno, quando unusquisque sedit sub vite et ficulnea sua, et de bonis terræ tractabant, quemadmodum primo libro Machabæorum circa finem plenius scriptum est. Porro in adventu Christi, quando per se ipsum atque Apostolos prædicavit, miracula fecit, et Spiritum Sanctum misit, copiosius adimpleta sunt hæc. Et consolabitur adhuc Dominus Sion, id est Synagogam et templi ministros. In monte etenim Sion reparatum est templum, et consolati sunt sacerdotes. Et eliget adhuc Jerusalem, id est, præ ceteris urbibus eam suo cultui dedicabit : quod factum est templo constructo, ad quod Judæi certis temporibus anni tenebantur venire, hostiasque offerre et Dominum invocare.
paras.en: Moreover the angel commands Zacharias: [[1:17|Cry yet, saying: Thus saith the Lord of hosts: My cities shall yet flow with good things|Adhuc clama, dicens : Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum : Adhuc affluent civitates meæ bonis]]: that is, after the return from Babylon the inhabitants of the cities of Juda shall abound in riches, and indeed, as regards the virtuous, in the spiritual gifts of grace too: which began to be fulfilled in the time of Zorobabel, Esdras and this Prophet[[1 Esd 1:1||]] [the margin gives 1 Esdr. i, etc., passim]; then after the victory of Judith[[Jdt 16:30||]], and in the time of the Machabees, above all under Simon, the priest and great prince, when [[1 Mach 14:12|every man sat under his vine, and under his fig tree|unusquisque sedit sub vite et ficulnea sua]], and [[1 Mach 14:9|treated together of the good things of the land|de bonis terræ tractabant]], as is written more fully toward the end of the first book of Machabees[[1 Mach 14:8||]]. Further, at the coming of Christ, when he preached by himself and by the Apostles, worked miracles, and sent the Holy Ghost[[Acts 2:1||]], these things were fulfilled more abundantly. [[1:17|and the Lord will yet comfort Sion|Et consolabitur adhuc Dominus Sion]], that is, the Synagogue and the ministers of the temple. For on mount Sion the temple was restored, and the priests were comforted. [[1:17|and he will yet choose Jerusalem|Et eliget adhuc Jerusalem]], that is, he will dedicate it to his worship before the other cities: which was done when the temple was built, to which the Jews were bound to come at certain times of the year, to offer victims and call upon the Lord.

paras.t: Præterea introducitur alia revelatio prophetalis de regnorum Judæis adversantium repressione. Et levavi ego Zacharias oculos meos interiores, et vidi, visione imaginaria; et ecce quatuor cornua vidi in spiritu. Et dixi ad angelum qui loquebatur in me : Quid sunt hæc? id est, quid significant? Et dixit ad me : Hæc sunt cornua, id est, per cornua ista significantur quatuor regna, quæ ventilaverunt Judam, id est regnum ac populum Judæorum, et Israel et Jerusalem, tribus Israel de propria terra expellendo, ipsamque Jerusalem devastando. Prædicta autem regna intelliguntur Chaldæi et Persæ, quantum ad reges Persarum adversantes Judæis; Græci quoque, præsertim tempore Antiochi, et Romani. Verumtamen, quum tempore Romanorum, post Christi passionem fuerint Judæi finaliter a Deo relicti, nec [jam] populus ejus propter Christi occisionem et abnegationem; nec regnum Romanum destructum fuerit eo quod Judæos vastavit : arbitror loco Romanorum Assyrios, vel alios quosdam aptius posse intelligi.
paras.en: Next another prophetic revelation is brought in, about the repressing of the kingdoms hostile to the Jews. [[1:18|And I lifted up|Et levavi]], I Zacharias, [[1:18|my eyes|oculos meos]] within, [[1:18|and saw|et vidi]], by an imaginary vision; [[1:18|and behold four horns|et ecce quatuor cornua]] I saw in the spirit. [[1:19|And I said to the angel that spoke in me: What are these|Et dixi ad angelum qui loquebatur in me : Quid sunt hæc]]? that is, what do they signify? [[1:19|And he said to me: These are the horns|Et dixit ad me : Hæc sunt cornua]], that is, by these horns are signified four kingdoms, [[1:19|that have scattered Juda|quæ ventilaverunt Judam]] [*ventilaverunt*, literally "have winnowed"], that is, the kingdom and people of the Jews, [[1:19|and Israel, and Jerusalem|et Israel et Jerusalem]], by driving the tribes of Israel out of their own land and laying waste Jerusalem itself. Now the aforesaid kingdoms are understood to be the Chaldeans, and the Persians as regards those kings of the Persians who were hostile to the Jews; the Greeks also, especially in the time of Antiochus; and the Romans. However, since in the time of the Romans, after the passion of Christ, the Jews were finally abandoned by God and were no longer his people, because of the slaying and the denial of Christ[[Dan 9:26||]][[Dan 9:27||]], and since the Roman kingdom was not destroyed for having laid waste the Jews, I think that in place of the Romans the Assyrians, or some others, may more fitly be understood.

paras.t: Et ostendit mihi Dominus quatuor fabros, id est similitudines eorum : sicut ostendit regi Ægypti boves et spicas, regique Babylonis auream statuam. Illis tamen non dedit intelligentiam visionis, quemadmodum Zachariæ, ut subditur. Et dixi ad angelum in me loquentem, qui in persona Dei loquebatur ad me : Quid isti quatuor fabri veniunt facere? Qui ait, dicens : Hæc sunt cornua quæ ventilaverunt Judam (hic repetit quod jam dixit de cornibus, ut clarius ostendat quod de fabris Propheta quæsivit) per singulos viros, unumquemque Judæorum in manus eorum venientium affligendo ; et nemo eorum, scilicet Judæorum, levavit caput suum, id est, resistere potuit adversariis suis. Et venerunt isti, utpote quatuor fabri, deterrere ea, id est regna præfata reprimere, ut dejiciant cornua gentium, id est, regna ista gentilium deprimant. Assyriorum enim et Chaldæorum regnum ante prophetiam istam defecit; postea quoque regnum Persarum atque Græcorum. Sed regnum Romanum non est propter Judæorum vastitatem dejectum, imo in Christo feliciter exaltatum. Vel si dejectum dicatur, quoniam Christo subjectum, hæc est bona dejectio, nec pro peccato inflicta. Quæ levaverunt cornu, id est potestatem suam, super terram Juda, id est contra Judæos, ut dispergerent eam, id est habitantes in ea. Itaque per fabros significabantur angelicæ potestates, divinæ jussionis exsecutores, qui venerunt superborum regna destruere, et populum Dei recuperare.
paras.en: [[1:20|And the Lord shewed me four smiths|Et ostendit mihi Dominus quatuor fabros]], that is, likenesses of them, as he showed the king of Egypt the kine and the ears of corn[[Gen 41:1||]], and the king of Babylon the golden statue[[Dan 2:31||]]. Yet to them he did not give the understanding of the vision, as he did to Zacharias, as follows. [[1:21|And I said|Et dixi]] to the angel speaking in me, who spoke to me in the person of God: [[1:21|What come these|Quid isti]] four smiths [[1:21|to do|veniunt facere]]? [[1:21|and he spoke, saying: These are the horns which have scattered Juda|Qui ait, dicens : Hæc sunt cornua quæ ventilaverunt Judam]] (here he repeats what he has already said of the horns, to show more clearly what the Prophet asked about the smiths) [[1:21|every man apart|per singulos viros]], afflicting each one of the Jews who came into their hands; [[1:21|and none of them|et nemo eorum]], that is, of the Jews, [[1:21|lifted up his head|levavit caput suum]], that is, could resist his enemies. [[1:21|and these are come|Et venerunt isti]], namely the four smiths, [[1:21|to fray them|deterrere ea]] [to *fray* is to frighten: Latin *deterrere*], that is, to repress the aforesaid kingdoms, [[1:21|to cast down the horns of the nations|ut dejiciant cornua gentium]], that is, to bring down these kingdoms of the Gentiles. For the kingdom of the Assyrians and Chaldeans had failed before this prophecy; afterwards also the kingdom of the Persians and that of the Greeks. But the Roman kingdom was not cast down for laying waste the Jews; rather it was happily exalted in Christ. Or if it is said to be cast down because it was made subject to Christ, this is a good casting down, and not inflicted for sin. [[1:21|that have lifted up the horn|Quæ levaverunt cornu]], that is, their power, [[1:21|upon the land of Juda|super terram Juda]], that is, against the Jews, [[1:21|to scatter it|ut dispergerent eam]], that is, those dwelling in it. So by the smiths were signified the angelic powers, executors of the divine command, who came to destroy the kingdoms of the proud and to recover the people of God.

paras.t: Postremo, per quatuor cornua memorata, intelligi possunt persecutores populi Israel, qui eum a quatuor partibus mundi invaserunt.
paras.en: Lastly, by the four horns mentioned may be understood the persecutors of the people of Israel, who attacked it from the four quarters of the world.

1.title: De spirituali ejusdem capituli primi intelligentia.
1.title_en: On the spiritual understanding of the same first chapter.

paras.t: FACTUM est verbum Domini ad Zachariam filium Barachiæ, filium Addo. Zacharias interpretatur memoria Domini. Itaque ad eum qui memor est Domini Dei sui, qui meditatur in lege Domini die ac nocte, qui ponit Deum sicut signaculum super cor suum, et revelata facie gloriam Domini speculatur, cum Psalmista decantans, Memor fui Dei, et delectatus sum : ad istum, inquam, fit verbum Dei, quia talis illuminatur a Deo, et unctio docet eum, ita ut dicere possit : Benedicam Dominum qui tribuit mihi intellectum; et rursus : Dominus illuminatio mea et salus mea. Is demum Barachiæ, id est divinæ benedictionis, est filius, quoniam Barachias benedictio Domini interpretatur. Recordatio etenim Dei, ex gratia cœlestis benedictionis emanat, quoniam actualis memoria Dei ex Spiritus Sancti motione procedit, sicut et quælibet actio meritoria. Insuper Zacharias iste est filius Addo, qui interpretatur testimonium ejus, quatenus Christus testimonium bonum perhibeat ei, confitendo eum coram Patre cœlesti et angelis ejus; ipse quoque divinæ virtuti in omnibus attestetur, et Deum in cunctis zelo veritatis honoret, sitque de eorum catalogo quibus per Isaiam Dominus dicit : Vos testes mei estis.
paras.en: [[1:1|the word of the Lord came to Zechariah the son of Barachias, the son of Addo|FACTUM est verbum Domini ad Zachariam filium Barachiæ, filium Addo]]. Zacharias is interpreted *memory of the Lord*. To him, then, who is mindful of the Lord his God [the margin gives Ps. lxxxvi, 4, which does not fit ("I will be mindful of Rahab"); perhaps Ps 76:4, quoted just below, is meant], who meditates on the law of the Lord day and night[[Ps 1:2||]], who sets God as a seal upon his heart[[Cant 8:6||]], and with open face beholds the glory of the Lord[[2 Cor 3:18||]], singing with the Psalmist, [[Ps 76:4|I remembered God, and was delighted|Memor fui Dei, et delectatus sum]]: to such a one, I say, the word of God comes, because such a man is enlightened by God, and the unction teaches him[[1 John 2:27||]], so that he can say: [[Ps 15:7|I will bless the Lord, who hath given me understanding|Benedicam Dominum qui tribuit mihi intellectum]]; and again: [[Ps 26:1|The Lord is my light and my salvation|Dominus illuminatio mea et salus mea]]. He is, moreover, the son of Barachias, that is, of the divine blessing, since Barachias is interpreted *blessing of the Lord*. For the remembrance of God flows from the grace of heavenly blessing, since the actual remembrance of God [*actualis memoria*, that is, God actually called to mind in the act of thinking, not merely kept in the memory as a habit] proceeds from the motion of the Holy Ghost, as does every meritorious act. Further, this Zacharias is the son of Addo, which is interpreted *his witness*: so that Christ may bear good witness to him, confessing him before the heavenly Father and his angels[[Luke 12:8||]]; and that he himself also may bear witness to the divine power in all things, and honour God in all things with zeal for the truth, and be of the number of those to whom the Lord says through Isaias: [[Is 44:8|you are my witnesses|Vos testes mei estis]].

paras.t: Itaque per hujuscemodi Zachariam ait Deus Ecclesiæ : Iratus est Dominus, scilicet ego Deus, super patres vestros, id est præcedentes Christianos, qui fidem suam vita ac moribus non approbarunt. Hoc Dominus ait, ut posteriores sint cautiores, ne eis contingat quod patribus suis evenit. Nempe felix, quem faciunt aliena damna peritum; et pestilente flagellato, sapiens, imo et stultus, sapientior erit, ut Salomon docet. Nam et ideo Deus in præsenti vita quosdam graviter manifesteque punit, ut illorum exemplo alii terreantur, corrigantur, salventur.
paras.en: Through such a Zacharias, then, God says to the Church: [[1:2|The Lord hath been exceeding angry|Iratus est Dominus]], that is, I, God, [[1:2|with your fathers|super patres vestros]], that is, the Christians who went before, who did not prove their faith by their life and conduct. The Lord says this so that those who come after may be more careful, lest there befall them what befell their fathers. For happy is he whom the harms of others make wise; and [[Prov 19:25|The wicked man being scourged|pestilente flagellato]], the wise man, nay even [[Prov 19:25|the fool shall be wiser|stultus, sapientior erit]], as Solomon teaches. And this is why God in the present life punishes some heavily and openly: that by their example others may be frightened, corrected and saved.

paras.t: Et dices ad eos. Qui enim modo præfato memor est Dei, aptus est mitti a Deo ad insinuandum proximis verbum Dei, ut de plenitudine ejus accipiant alii, et memoriam abundantiæ suavitatis divinæ, quam in secreto ex Dei contemplatione sortitus est, eructet et aliis, secundum quod Petrus in prima sua ait Canonica : Unusquisque sicut accepit gratiam, in alterutrum illam administrantes.
paras.en: [[1:3|And thou shalt say to them|Et dices ad eos]]. For he who is mindful of God in the way described is fit to be sent by God to make the word of God known to his neighbours, so that others may receive [[John 1:16|of his fulness|de plenitudine ejus]], and that he may pour out to others also [[Ps 144:7|the memory of the abundance|memoriam abundantiæ]] of the divine sweetness which he has gained in secret from the contemplation of God [*eructet*, "belch forth", the word of the Psalm, which the Douay-Rheims renders "publish"]; according to what Peter says in his first Canonical Epistle: [[1 Pet 4:10|As every man hath received grace, ministering the same one to another|Unusquisque sicut accepit gratiam, in alterutrum illam administrantes]].

paras.t: Hæc dicit Dominus : Convertimini ad me. Incessabiliter per sacræ Scripturæ lectionem, prædicationem et recordationem hortatur nos Deus, ut convertamur ad ipsum, omnia ista carnalia, terrena, vilissima contemnendo, ipsique summo, superessentiali, immenso et perfecto bono integerrima mente fortiter adhærendo : in quo utique est omnium divitiarum, deliciarum, et honestatis superinfinitissima plenitudo. Quum enim Deus sit primum et summum appetibile, honorabile, ac formidabile, ipsum primo et summe desiderare, honorare, ac formidare debemus; ipse quoque esse debet nobis causa et ratio amandi seu appetendi, venerandi ac metuendi, quidquid citra eum desideramus, amamus, honoramus, aut formidamus, quatenus omnes nostri cordis affectus sint ordinati, reducti, ac adunati in ipsum : quo facto, veraciter dicere possumus, Confitebor tibi, Domine, in toto corde meo.
paras.en: [[1:3|Thus saith the Lord|Hæc dicit Dominus]]: [[1:3|Turn ye to me|Convertimini ad me]]. Unceasingly, through the reading, preaching and remembrance of sacred Scripture, God exhorts us to turn to him, despising all these carnal, earthly and most worthless things, and cleaving strongly, with a wholly undivided mind, to him, the highest, superessential, immense and perfect good: in whom indeed is the more than infinite fullness of all riches, delights and honour. For since God is the first and highest object of desire, of honour and of fear, we ought to desire, honour and fear him first and above all; and he also ought to be for us the cause and reason of loving or desiring, of revering and fearing, whatever below him we desire, love, honour or fear, so that all the affections of our heart may be set in order, led back and gathered into one in him: and when this is done, we can truly say, [[Ps 9:2|I will give praise to thee, O Lord, with my whole heart|Confitebor tibi, Domine, in toto corde meo]][[Ps 137:1||]].

paras.t: Et convertar ad vos. Tanta equidem est munificentia atque benignitas bonitatis divinæ, ut quacumque hora peccator ex animo ingemuerit, vel homo quod in se est fecerit, Deus gratiam mox infundat : idcirco de nullo viatore est desperandum. Præterea verbum istud Dei nostri dulcissimum, Convertar ad vos, et tanta Dei pronitas ad ignoscendum, ad succurrendum atque salvandum nos, quantumcumque inique egerimus, dummodo modo prædicto convertamur ad ipsum, merito inflammare nos debet ad admirandum ac diligendum et imitandum viscera caritatis et misericordiæ Dei nostri, ut simus imitatores Dei sicut filii carissimi, et ambulemus in dilectione sicut et Christus dilexit nos, nec aliquam a proximo aversionem admittamus.
paras.en: [[1:3|and I will turn to you|Et convertar ad vos]]. So great indeed is the munificence and kindness of the divine goodness that at whatever hour the sinner groans from his heart, or a man does what is in him [that is, does what lies in his own power, the condition on which, in the schoolmen's phrase, God does not deny grace], God at once pours in grace: and therefore no wayfarer [*viator*, one still on the way in this life, not yet at the end] is to be despaired of. Moreover, this most sweet word of our God, [[1:3|I will turn to you|Convertar ad vos]], and so great a readiness of God to pardon, to help and to save us, however wickedly we have acted, provided we turn to him in the way described, ought rightly to inflame us to admire, love and imitate the bowels of the charity and [[Luke 1:78|the mercy of our God|misericordiæ Dei nostri]], so that we may be [[Eph 5:1|followers of God, as most dear children|imitatores Dei sicut filii carissimi]], and [[Eph 5:2|walk in love, as Christ also hath loved us|ambulemus in dilectione sicut et Christus dilexit nos]], and admit no turning away from our neighbour.

paras.t: Denique viatoribus Dominus ait : Patres vestri ubi sunt et prophetæ? Hoc nobis incessanter pensandum est, quatenus, patrum et prædecessorum nostrorum obitum considerantes, et quo venerint ignorantes, quod item in æternum mansuri sint vel in summa gloria, vel in summa miseria, discamus vitæ præsentis vanitatem, fallaciam, brevitatem, periculositatem, incertitudinemque pensare ac spernere, et Deo cum omni reverentia et timore servire, dicendo : Ubi jam patres nostri, et ceteri qui ante pauca tempora nobiscum fuerunt? Ecce in momento sublati sunt, æternaliterque manebunt vel in tormentis inferni, vel in jucunditate cœlesti, prout in hac vita brevissima meruerunt. Prophetæ autem de quibus jam sermo, sunt qui, quod scribunt, docent seu prædicant, non observant : quorum damnatio justa est.
paras.en: Lastly, the Lord says to wayfarers: [[1:5|Your fathers, where are they? and the prophets|Patres vestri ubi sunt et prophetæ]]? This we must ponder unceasingly: so that, considering the death of our fathers and forebears, and not knowing where they have gone, and that they will likewise abide for ever either in the highest glory or in the deepest misery, we may learn to weigh and to despise the vanity, deceitfulness, brevity, perilousness and uncertainty of the present life, and to serve God with all reverence and fear, saying: Where now are our fathers, and the others who were with us a little while ago? Behold, in a moment they have been taken away, and they will abide eternally either in the torments of hell or in heavenly joy, according as they deserved in this most brief life. And the prophets of whom the text now speaks are those who do not keep what they write, teach or preach: and their condemnation is just.

paras.t: Præterea ait spiritualis hic Zacharias, Dei jugiter reminiscens : Vidi per noctem, id est cognitione obscura : nunc enim videmus per speculum in ænigmate eum qui posuit tenebras latibulum suum; et ecce vir ascendens super equum rufum, id est, Christus Deus et homo, corpus humanum tempore passionis sanguine rubricatum, suæ divinitati adjungens, ipsoque ad nostram recuperandam salutem ministerialiter utens. De quo in Isaia habetur : Ecce Dominus ascendet super nubem levem; et rursus, Quare rubrum est indumentum tuum? Et ipse stabat inter myrteta, id est inter vetus ac novum Testamentum : quæ tanquam duo Cherubim versis vultibus respiciunt in ipsum, tanquam in propitiatorium, quoniam ipse veraciter est propitiatio pro peccatis nostris. Hæc autem testamenta cooperta sunt difficultatibus multis, tanquam densissimis foliis. Vel myrteta sunt omnes viri perfecti, in quorum medio Dominus commoratur : qui sunt bonus odor Dei, et fructus operum meritoriorum copiose producunt.
paras.en: Further, this spiritual Zacharias, ever mindful of God, says: [[1:8|I saw by night|Vidi per noctem]], that is, by a dark knowledge: for [[1 Cor 13:12|we see now through a glass in a dark manner|videmus per speculum in ænigmate]] him who [[Ps 17:12|made darkness his cover|posuit tenebras latibulum suum]]; [[1:8|and behold a man riding upon a red horse|et ecce vir ascendens super equum rufum]] [*ascendens*, literally "mounting", the word Isaias uses below], that is, Christ, God and man, joining to his divinity a human body reddened with blood at the time of the passion, and using it as an instrument to recover our salvation. Of whom we have in Isaias: [[Is 19:1|Behold the Lord will ascend upon a swift cloud|Ecce Dominus ascendet super nubem levem]]; and again, [[Is 63:2|Why then is thy apparel red?|Quare rubrum est indumentum tuum?]] [[1:8|and he stood among the myrtle trees|Et ipse stabat inter myrteta]], that is, between the Old and the New Testament: which, like the two Cherubim with their faces turned, look towards him as towards the propitiatory [that is, the mercy seat, the golden cover of the Ark between the Cherubim], since he truly [[1 John 2:2|is the propitiation for our sins|est propitiatio pro peccatis nostris]]. And these Testaments are covered with many difficulties, as with the thickest leaves. Or the myrtle trees are all perfect men, in whose midst the Lord dwells: who are [[2 Cor 2:15|the good odour|bonus odor]] of God, and bring forth the fruits of meritorious works abundantly.

paras.t: Et post eum equi rufi, varii, et albi. Equi rufi sunt martyres sancti, qui laverunt stolas suas in sanguine Agni. Equi varii sunt confessores diversis gratiæ charismatibus adornati. Equi albi sunt virgines puritatis candore splendentes.
paras.en: [[1:8|and behind him were horses, red, speckled, and white|Et post eum equi rufi, varii, et albi]]. The red horses are the holy martyrs, who [[Apoc 7:14|have washed their robes|laverunt stolas suas]] [[Apoc 7:14|in the blood of the Lamb|in sanguine Agni]]. The speckled horses are the confessors, adorned with the diverse gifts of grace. The white horses are the virgins, shining with the whiteness of purity.

paras.t: Istis, præsertim Apostolis, qui et martyres exstiterunt, jussit Dominus ut perambularent terram, verbum Dei prædicando ubique, juxta illud : Euntes in mundum universum, prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ; et alibi, Eritis mihi testes in omni Judæa et Samaria, et usque ad fines terræ. In omnem quippe terram exivit sonus eorum.
paras.en: These, and above all the Apostles, who were martyrs too, the Lord commanded [[1:10|to walk through the earth|ut perambularent terram]], preaching the word of God everywhere, according to that: [[Mark 16:15|Go ye into the whole world and preach the gospel to every creature|Euntes in mundum universum, prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ]]; and elsewhere, [[Acts 1:8|you shall be witnesses unto me|Eritis mihi testes]] [[Acts 1:8|in all Judea, and Samaria, and even to the uttermost part of the earth|in omni Judæa et Samaria, et usque ad fines terræ]]. For [[Ps 18:5|their sound hath gone forth into all the earth|In omnem quippe terram exivit sonus eorum]].

paras.t: Denique Sancti hi, injuncto sibi prædicationis officio digne completo, revertuntur ad Christum, dicentes : Perambulavimus terram, et ecce omnis terra habitatur, et quiescit : id est, ubique terrarum fides catholica disseminata est, et homines ad Deum conversi, inhabitantur a Spiritu Sancto, atque in spe bona quiescunt.
paras.en: Lastly these Saints, having worthily fulfilled the office of preaching laid upon them, return to Christ, saying: [[1:11|We have walked through the earth, and behold all the earth is inhabited, and is at rest|Perambulavimus terram, et ecce omnis terra habitatur, et quiescit]]: that is, the Catholic faith has been sown everywhere in the world, and men, converted to God, are indwelt by the Holy Ghost, and rest in good hope.

paras.t: Tunc vir qui stabat inter myrteta, videlicet Christus magni consilii Angelus, orat Deum Patrem, secundum quod homo et mediator, pro militanti Ecclesia, dicens : Usquequo tu non misereberis Jerusalem et urbium Juda, id est universali Ecclesiæ, et particularibus congregationibus electorum confitentium tibi, perducendo eos ad beatitudinem consummatam, quibus iratus es, permittendo eos in sæculo isto multipliciter tribulari, ita ut quasi iratus appareas?
paras.en: Then [[1:10|the man that stood among the myrtle trees|vir qui stabat inter myrteta]], namely Christ, the Angel of great counsel[[Is 9:6||]] [the Septuagint reading of Isaias 9:6; the Vulgate has "Counsellor"], prays to God the Father, as man and mediator, for the Church militant, saying: [[1:12|how long wilt thou not have mercy on Jerusalem, and on the cities of Juda|Usquequo tu non misereberis Jerusalem et urbium Juda]], that is, on the universal Church, and on the particular congregations of the elect who confess thee, by bringing them to consummate beatitude, [[1:12|with which thou hast been angry|quibus iratus es]], by permitting them to be troubled in many ways in this world, so that thou seemest as it were angry?

paras.t: Ad hanc precem respondit Deus verba bona ac consolatoria, scilicet quod cito liberabuntur, et ista tribulatio atque dilatio gloriæ ipsis perutilis est.
paras.en: To this prayer God answered [[1:13|good words|verba bona]] and [[1:13|comfortable words|consolatoria]]: namely, that they will soon be set free, and that this tribulation and this delay of their glory is most profitable to them.

paras.t: Hæc dicit Dominus : Zelatus sum Jerusalem, id est Ecclesiam divinæ pacis visione aliqualiter nunc gaudentem, et Sion, id est animas divinorum speculatrices. Jerusalem enim visio pacis, et Sion speculatio interpretatur. Zelo magno : sic enim Deus dilexit mundum, ut Filium suum unigenitum daret. Ideo quos amat zelo paterno, arguit et castigat.
paras.en: [[1:14|Thus saith the Lord|Hæc dicit Dominus]]: [[1:14|I am zealous for Jerusalem|Zelatus sum Jerusalem]], that is, the Church, which even now in some measure rejoices in the vision of divine peace, [[1:14|and Sion|et Sion]], that is, the souls that contemplate divine things. For Jerusalem is interpreted *vision of peace*, and Sion *watching* [*speculatio*, a looking out from a height; hence the souls *speculatrices*, contemplatives]. [[1:14|with a great zeal|Zelo magno]]: for [[John 3:16|God so loved the world, as to give his only begotten Son|Deus dilexit mundum, ut Filium suum unigenitum daret]]. Therefore those whom he loves with a father's zeal, he rebukes and chastises[[Apoc 3:19||]].

paras.t: Et ira magna ego irascor super gentes opulentas, id est electorum ac justorum persecutores, ac divites qui consolationem suam jam habent, et bonos impia intentione angustant. Et tamen per eos Deus nunc purgat corrigitque electos : quibus purgatis, illi projiciuntur in tartarum, quemadmodum filio emendato, virga projicitur mox in ignem.
paras.en: [[1:15|And I am angry with a great anger with the wealthy nations|Et ira magna ego irascor super gentes opulentas]], that is, the persecutors of the elect and of the just, and the rich who already have their consolation[[Luke 6:24||]], and who with wicked intent oppress the good. And yet through them God now purges and corrects the elect: and once these have been purged, those are cast into hell, just as, once the son has been corrected, the rod is straightway thrown into the fire.

paras.t: Sicque Dominus revertitur ad Jerusalem in misericordiis, dando electis piissima gratiæ dona pro tribulationibus quas tulerunt; et domus sua, videlicet cubiculum conscientiæ, ædificatur in eis, ita quod Deus clementissime et libenter corda eorum inhabitat. Tunc demum perpendiculum, id est recta consideratio atque discussio justa conversationis, extenditur super Jerusalem, id est Ecclesiam : ita quod Spiritus Sanctus illustrat fideles ad considerandum, dirigendum, et judicandum se ipsos et omnia opera vitæ suæ, secundum rectitudinem æquitatis, divinæque legis rectitudinem (al. certitudinem).
paras.en: And so the Lord returns [[1:16|to Jerusalem in mercies|ad Jerusalem in misericordiis]], giving the elect most loving gifts of grace for the tribulations they have borne; and his house, namely the chamber of conscience, is built in them, so that God most mercifully and willingly dwells in their hearts. Then at length [[1:16|the building line|perpendiculum]] [*perpendiculum*, the plumb line], that is, a right consideration and a just examination of one's way of life, is stretched forth [[1:16|upon Jerusalem|super Jerusalem]], that is, the Church: so that the Holy Ghost enlightens the faithful to consider, direct and judge themselves and all the works of their life according to the rightness of equity and the rightness of the divine law [a footnote in the edition gives the variant *certitudinem*, "certainty", for this second *rectitudinem*].

paras.t: Adhuc clama, dicens : Hæc dicit Dominus : Adhuc affluent civitates meæ bonis, id est, Ecclesiæ particulares seu religiones, claustra sive collegia, donis et gratiis spiritualibus, magna devotione et regularibus observantiis exuberabunt. Hoc Deus frequenter tempore evangelicæ legis implevit, reformando per quosdam sanctissimos patres statum Ecclesiæ, saltem in parte.
paras.en: [[1:17|Cry yet, saying|Adhuc clama, dicens]]: [[1:17|Thus saith the Lord|Hæc dicit Dominus]]: [[1:17|My cities shall yet flow with good things|Adhuc affluent civitates meæ bonis]], that is, the particular Churches, or religious orders, cloisters or colleges, will abound in spiritual gifts and graces, in great devotion and in regular observances. This God has often fulfilled in the time of the law of the Gospel, reforming the state of the Church, at least in part, through certain most holy fathers.

paras.t: Et consolabitur adhuc Dominus Sion, id est animas fidelium in divinorum speculatione consistentes : quæ lapsum Ecclesiæ vel propria mala deplorant, quas Deus nonnunquam dulciter visitat, afficit, recreat, earumque preces exaudit, et quosdam meritis earum convertit. Hinc ad Corinthios dicit Apostolus : Benedictus Deus, Pater misericordiarum, et Deus totius consolationis, qui consolatur nos in omni tribulatione nostra ; quoniam sicut abundant passiones Christi in nobis, ita et per Christum abundat consolatio nostra ; et sicut socii passionum sumus, sic erimus et socii consolationis. Non enim permittit misericors Deus sibi devotos immoderanter et super vires affligi ; virtuosam quoque tristitiam spiritualis delectatio concomitatur, præsertim quum omni actui virtutis annexa dicatur delectatio bona, connaturalis, et propria. Et eliget adhuc Jerusalem, id est, præ ceteris universis salutem gratiamque impendit Ecclesiæ Christi, extra quam nemo salvatur. Hoc ad Ecclesiam referri potest pro tempore Antichristi, quando Elias adveniens restituet omnia, et Judæi convertentur ad fidem, magnaque valde erit Christianorum devotio, Antichristo occiso.
paras.en: [[1:17|and the Lord will yet comfort Sion|Et consolabitur adhuc Dominus Sion]], that is, the souls of the faithful who abide in the contemplation of divine things: who lament the fall of the Church or their own sins, whom God sometimes sweetly visits, moves and refreshes, and whose prayers he hears, and some he converts by their merits. Hence the Apostle says to the Corinthians: [[2 Cor 1:3|Blessed be the God|Benedictus Deus]], [[2 Cor 1:3|the Father of mercies and the God of all comfort|Pater misericordiarum, et Deus totius consolationis]], [[2 Cor 1:4|Who comforteth us in all our tribulation|qui consolatur nos in omni tribulatione nostra]]; [[2 Cor 1:5|For as the sufferings of Christ abound in us: so also by Christ doth our comfort abound|quoniam sicut abundant passiones Christi in nobis, ita et per Christum abundat consolatio nostra]]; and as we are partakers of the sufferings, so shall we be also of the consolation[[2 Cor 1:7||]] [Denis puts the Apostle's "you" into the first person]. For the merciful God does not allow those devoted to him to be afflicted beyond measure and beyond their strength; and spiritual delight accompanies virtuous sorrow, especially since a good delight, connatural and proper to it, is said to be joined to every act of virtue. [[1:17|and he will yet choose Jerusalem|Et eliget adhuc Jerusalem]], that is, above all others he bestows salvation and grace on the Church of Christ, outside which no one is saved. This can be referred to the Church in the time of Antichrist, when Elias shall come and restore all things[[Matt 17:11||]], and the Jews shall be converted to the faith, and very great shall be the devotion of Christians, once Antichrist has been slain.

paras.t: Et levavi oculos meos, et vidi ; et ecce quatuor cornua. Sic dum spiritualiter oculos mentis erigimus, statum et tentationes fidelium considerantes, adspicimus quatuor cornua.
