Quæ ventilaverunt et ventilant jugiter Judam, id est Domino confitentes, et Israel, id est contemplativos, et Jerusalem, id est Ecclesiam. Cornua ista, sunt contrariæ potestates, hostes nostræ salutis : de quibus ait Apostolus, quod sit nobis colluctatio adversus principatus et potestates, adversus mundi rectores tenebrarum harum, contra spiritualia nequitiæ in cœlestibus. Vel cornua ista, sunt mundus, diabolus, caro, et propria voluntas, vel quatuor animæ passiones principales, vel spiritus superbiæ, spiritus fornicationis, spiritus cupiditatis, spiritusque invidiæ ; quibus homines præcipue tentantur, pulsantur, et impelluntur, ita ut nemo levet caput, id est, propriis viribus eis prævaleat. Vel cornua ista, sunt hæretici, schismatici, tyranni, et generaliter omnes justorum persecutores.
paras.en: [[1:18|And I lifted up my eyes, and saw: and behold four horns|Et levavi oculos meos, et vidi ; et ecce quatuor cornua]]. So, when we raise the eyes of the mind spiritually, considering the state and the temptations of the faithful, we behold four horns, [[1:19|that have scattered|Quæ ventilaverunt]], and continually scatter, [[1:19|Juda|Judam]], that is, those who confess the Lord [Juda means *confession* or *praise*], [[1:19|and Israel|et Israel]], that is, the contemplatives [Israel being taken as *a man seeing God*], [[1:19|and Jerusalem|et Jerusalem]], that is, the Church. These horns are the adverse powers, the enemies of our salvation: of which the Apostle says that [[Eph 6:12|our wrestling is|nobis colluctatio]] [[Eph 6:12|against principalities and powers, against the rulers of the world of this darkness, against the spirits of wickedness in the high places|adversus principatus et potestates, adversus mundi rectores tenebrarum harum, contra spiritualia nequitiæ in cœlestibus]]. Or these horns are the world, the devil, the flesh, and self-will; or the four principal passions of the soul [joy, sorrow, hope and fear]; or the spirit of pride, the spirit of fornication, the spirit of covetousness, and the spirit of envy: by which men are chiefly tempted, assailed and driven, so that no one lifts up his head[[1:21||]], that is, prevails against them by his own strength. Or these horns are heretics, schismatics, tyrants, and in general all persecutors of the just.

paras.t: Et ostendit mihi Dominus quatuor fabros. Isti quatuor fabri, qui venerunt deterrere atque dejicere cornua jam prædicta, sunt quatuor Evangelistæ, quorum doctrina omnis adversariorum perversitas superatur, et quod in anima per peccata destructum est, reparatur. Sed et quatuor Doctores Ecclesiæ, et quatuor virtutes cardinales, aliquo modo per fabros istos intelligi possunt.
paras.en: [[1:20|And the Lord shewed me four smiths|Et ostendit mihi Dominus quatuor fabros]]. These four smiths, who [[1:21|are come to fray them|venerunt deterrere]] [that is, to frighten them off] and [[1:21|to cast down the horns|dejicere cornua]] already spoken of, are the four Evangelists, by whose teaching all the perversity of the adversaries is overcome, and what was destroyed in the soul by sins is repaired. But the four Doctors of the Church, and the four cardinal virtues, may also in some way be understood by these smiths.

2.title: Expositio litteralis capituli secundi: Et levavi oculos meos, et vidi.
2.title_en: Literal exposition of the second chapter: And I lifted up my eyes, and saw.

paras.t: Rursus Dominus præostendit Prophetæ reædificationem urbium Juda. Et levavi oculos meos mentales per advertentiam diligentem, et vidi, visione imaginaria simul et intellectuali ; et ecce vir, id est, angelus in specie viri mihi apparuit. Dicuntque aliqui, quod fuit angelus qui in præcedenti capitulo fertur stetisse inter myrteta, videlicet Michael, præsertim quum angelus iste totius terræ ac populi curam gerere videatur, quasi præsidens Synagogæ. Et in manu ejus funiculus mensorum, id est talis qualem mensuratores locorum ac ædificiorum solent habere.
paras.en: Again the Lord shows the Prophet beforehand the rebuilding of the cities of Juda. [[2:1|And I lifted up my eyes|Et levavi oculos meos]], the eyes of the mind, by careful attention, [[2:1|and saw|et vidi]], by a vision at once imaginary and intellectual [that is, a vision both of images formed in the imagination and of understanding in the mind]; [[2:1|and behold a man|et ecce vir]], that is, an angel appeared to me in the likeness of a man. And some say that it was the angel who in the preceding chapter is said to have stood among the myrtle trees[[Zach 1:8||]], namely Michael, especially since this angel seems to have the care of the whole land and people, as one presiding over the Synagogue. [[2:1|with a measuring line in his hand|Et in manu ejus funiculus mensorum]], that is, such a line as measurers of places and buildings are wont to have.

paras.t: Et dixi, cupiens informari de ignotis : Quo tu vadis? Et dixit ad me : Ut metiar Jerusalem, et videam quanta sit latitudo ejus, et quanta longitudo ejus. Per hanc mensurationem Jerusalem metropolis in Judæa et aliorum locorum ejus, significabatur recuperatio civitatum istarum, atque reductio populi ad pristinum statum, etsi non per omnia parem. Metiebatur quoque angelus loca hæc, non quod eorum quantitatem ignoravit ; sed ad instructionem Prophetæ humano more se habuit, quo solent mensurari ædificia secundum longum et latum, et loca eorum antequam construantur. Simile huic in Ezechiele legitur.
paras.en: [[2:2|And I said|Et dixi]], wishing to be informed of things unknown: [[2:2|Whither goest thou? and he said to me: To measure Jerusalem, and to see how great is the breadth thereof, and how great the length thereof|Quo tu vadis? Et dixit ad me : Ut metiar Jerusalem, et videam quanta sit latitudo ejus, et quanta longitudo ejus]]. By this measuring of Jerusalem, the chief city in Judæa, and of its other places, was signified the recovery of those cities and the bringing back of the people to their former state, though not one equal to it in all things. And the angel measured these places, not because he did not know their size; but for the Prophet's instruction he behaved in the human manner, in which buildings, and the places for them, are wont to be measured by length and breadth before they are built. Something like this is read in Ezechiel[[Ezech 40:3||]].

paras.t: Et ecce angelus qui loquebatur in me, per quem mihi familiarius dicebantur futura, meque immediate instruxit, egrediebatur, ut extra me aliquid operaretur. Angeli enim sunt in loco definitive : nam ubi operantur, ibi sunt. Denique aliqui asserunt, quod egrediebatur, ut ab angelo superioris ordinis aliquam novam de futuris revelationem acciperet. Quibus obviare videtur, quod secundum doctores, localis distantia mutuam angelorum locutionem et illuminationem non impedit, quia ut ait Augustinus, Quod in corporalibus facit situs, hoc in spiritualibus efficit ordo. Et alius angelus egrediebatur, forte de cœlo descendens, vel aliunde de aliquo exiens, in occursum ejus.
paras.en: [[2:3|And behold the angel that spoke in me|Et ecce angelus qui loquebatur in me]], through whom things to come were told me more familiarly, and who instructed me directly, [[2:3|went forth|egrediebatur]], to work something outside me. For angels are in a place definitively [that is, by being present where they act, not by occupying space as bodies do]: for where they work, there they are. Again, some assert that he went forth in order to receive some new revelation of things to come from an angel of a higher order. Against these seems to stand the fact that, according to the doctors, distance of place does not hinder the speech and enlightenment of angels one with another; for, as Augustine says, What position does in bodily things, order does in spiritual ones. [[2:3|and another angel went out|et alius angelus egrediebatur]], coming down perhaps from heaven, or going out from some other place, [[2:3|to meet him|in occursum ejus]].

paras.t: Et dixit ad eum : Curre, loquere ad puerum istum Zachariam. Septuaginta transtulerunt, Loquere adolescentulo illi : quia ut ait Hieronymus, comparatione angelicæ dignitatis, omnis humana conditio et natura quasi pueritia est. Vel puerum dicit propter puritatem ejus et innocentiam. Ex quo constat, quod angeli superiores mittunt et illuminant inferiores, quemadmodum S. Dionysius scribit.
paras.en: [[2:4|And he said to him: Run, speak to this young man|Et dixit ad eum : Curre, loquere ad puerum istum]], Zacharias. The Septuagint translated, Speak to that youth: because, as Jerome says, in comparison with the dignity of the angels, all human condition and nature is as it were childhood. Or he says *puer* ["boy"; the Douay-Rheims has "young man"] because of his purity and innocence [a play on *puer* and *puritas*]. From this it is clear that the higher angels send and enlighten the lower, as St. Dionysius writes.

paras.t: Dicens : Absque muro habitabitur Jerusalem præ multitudine hominum et jumentorum in medio ejus exsistentium. Istud, ut refert Hieronymus, præstolantur Judæi corporaliter in adventu sui Messiæ implendum. Quibus objici potest illud Isaiæ, quod etiam ipsi corporaliter putant in Messiæ adventu futurum, Occupabit salus muros tuos, et alia multa quæ Isaias atque Ezechiel de muris civitatis conscribunt : non quod ista corporaliter sint intelligenda, sed quod litterales atque carnales Judæi figmenta sua salvare non queunt. Est igitur sensus, quod Jerusalem habitanda esset in magna securitate et abundantia, quasi muris non indigeret. Et ita est locutio figurativa ac hyperbolica, ad insinuandum inopinatam prosperitatem ac multiplicationem Jerusalem in ædificiis, hominibus ac jumentis.
paras.en: [[2:4|saying|Dicens]]: [[2:4|Jerusalem shall be inhabited without walls, by reason of the multitude of men, and of the beasts in the midst thereof|Absque muro habitabitur Jerusalem præ multitudine hominum et jumentorum in medio ejus]]. This, as Jerome relates, the Jews await to be fulfilled bodily at the coming of their Messias. Against them may be set the words of Isaias which they themselves also think will come to pass bodily at the Messias's coming, [[Is 60:18|salvation shall possess thy walls|Occupabit salus muros tuos]], and many other things that Isaias[[Is 49:16||]][[Is 62:6||]] and Ezechiel[[Ezech 40:5||]] write about the walls of the city [the margin gives "Ezech. xi. et seq."; the walls are measured in Ezech. xl and following]: not that these are to be understood bodily, but because the literal-minded and carnal Jews cannot save their fancies. The sense, then, is that Jerusalem was to be inhabited in great security and plenty, as though it had no need of walls. And so it is a figurative and hyperbolic way of speaking, to suggest the unlooked-for prosperity and increase of Jerusalem in buildings, men and beasts.

paras.t: Et ego ero ei, ait Dominus, murus ignis in circuitu, id est fidelis protector ex omni parte, quamdiu mihi obedient ; et in gloria ero in medio ejus, id est, glorificabor per latriæ cultum ab inhabitantibus eam, eroque eis in gloriam, corda ipsorum lætificando, et ipsos magnifice exaltando.
paras.en: [[2:5|And I will be to it, saith the Lord, a wall of fire round about|Et ego ero ei, ait Dominus, murus ignis in circuitu]], that is, a faithful protector on every side, so long as they obey me; [[2:5|and I will be in glory in the midst thereof|et in gloria ero in medio ejus]], that is, I shall be glorified with the worship of *latria* [that is, the worship due to God alone] by those who dwell in it, and I shall be their glory, gladdening their hearts and exalting them magnificently.

paras.t: Consequenter dirigitur sermo Domini ad Judæos qui sponte in Chaldæa remanserant post reditum aliorum de Babylone sub Cyro. O, o, o, fugite de terra aquilonis, scilicet a Chaldæa, dicit Dominus : quoniam in quatuor ventos cœli dispersi vos, id est per quatuor plagas terræ, ex quibus principales venti erumpunt : qui dicuntur venti cœli, quia in aere flant. Deus enim per Assyrios et Chaldæos dispersit populum Judæorum per diversas mundi provincias. Et ex quatuor ventis colligam vos, id est, de prædictis locis vos congregabo atque in terram Juda reducam : juxta illud Ezechielis, Tollam quippe vos de gentibus, et congregabo vos de nationibus, et adducam vos in terram vestram.
paras.en: Next the word of the Lord is directed to the Jews who had stayed behind of their own will in Chaldæa after the return of the others from Babylon under Cyrus. [[2:6|O, O flee ye out of the land of the north|O, o, o, fugite de terra aquilonis]], namely from Chaldæa, [[2:6|saith the Lord|dicit Dominus]]: [[2:6|for I have scattered you into the four winds of heaven|quoniam in quatuor ventos cœli dispersi vos]], that is, through the four quarters of the earth, from which the chief winds break forth; and these are called winds of heaven because they blow in the air. For through the Assyrians and the Chaldeans God scattered the people of the Jews through the various provinces of the world. And from the four winds I will gather you [these words are not in the Vulgate or the Douay-Rheims; the Septuagint reads "from the four winds of heaven I will gather you"], that is, I will gather you from the places named and bring you back into the land of Juda: according to that saying of Ezechiel, [[Ezech 36:24|For I will take you from among the Gentiles, and will gather you together out of all the countries, and will bring you into your own land|Tollam quippe vos de gentibus, et congregabo vos de nationibus, et adducam vos in terram vestram]].

paras.t: O Sion, id est, plebs Judæorum, fuge, quæ habitas apud filiam Babylonis, id est, ad propriam terram revertere, quæ in regione Babyloniæ demoraris. Dicitur autem gens illa, quamvis fuerint infideles, filia Dei, propter paternum amorem quo Deus amat humanam naturam, et item ratione creationis. Unde et in Isaia Dominus ait : Descende, sede in pulvere, filia Babylon.
paras.en: [[2:7|O Sion|O Sion]], that is, people of the Jews, [[2:7|flee, thou that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon|fuge, quæ habitas apud filiam Babylonis]], that is, return to thy own land, thou that tarriest in the region of Babylonia. Now that nation, though they were unbelievers, is called a daughter of God, because of the fatherly love with which God loves human nature, and likewise by reason of creation. Hence also in Isaias the Lord says: [[Is 47:1|Come down, sit in the dust|Descende, sede in pulvere]], O [[Is 47:1|daughter of Babylon|filia Babylon]].

paras.t: Quia hæc dicit Dominus exercituum : Post gloriam misit me ad gentes quæ spoliaverunt vos. Ecce hic ait Dominus exercituum, se missum a Domino, scilicet Filius a Patre. Nam secundum seriem litteræ, quod dictum est, Post gloriam misit me, non est verbum in persona Zachariæ prolatum, sed Dei perhibentis se mitti post gloriam : quod multipliciter explanatur. Hieronymus enim exponit, Post gloriam majestatis divinæ : non quod Filius illam amiserit, sed quod forma servi accepta, in humilitate apparuit. Sed tunc videretur ad tempus incarnationis hæc missio referenda. Quod aliqui concedentes, per gloriam hoc loco intelligunt excellentiam monarchiæ a Romanis adeptæ, præsertim a Cæsare Augusto, sub quo descriptus est orbis, et tunc natus est Christus. Sed verba sequentia non satis consonare videntur. Quidam vero per gloriam istam intelligunt dominationem Chaldæorum, post quam a rege Babylonis adeptam, missus est spirituali missione Filius a Patre ad gentes quæ spoliaverunt Judæos, videlicet ad Chaldæos, quos Persæ ac Medi virtute Filii Dei destruxerunt. Juxta quem modum de Filio Dei scriptum est in Sapientia : Dum medium silentium tenerent omnia, omnipotens sermo tuus, Domine, de cœlo exsiliens, a regalibus sedibus venit. Et loquitur ibi ad litteram de punitione Ægyptiorum. Porro quod Filio conveniat spiritualiter mitti, non solum per incarnationem et naturam assumptam, primo Sententiarum satis edocetur.
paras.en: [[2:8|For thus saith the Lord of hosts: After the glory he hath sent me to the nations that have robbed you|Quia hæc dicit Dominus exercituum : Post gloriam misit me ad gentes quæ spoliaverunt vos]]. See, here the Lord of hosts says that he is sent by the Lord, that is, the Son by the Father. For according to the sequence of the letter, what is said, [[2:8|After the glory he hath sent me|Post gloriam misit me]], is not a word spoken in the person of Zacharias, but of God declaring that he is sent after the glory; and this is explained in many ways. For Jerome expounds it: After the glory of the divine majesty; not that the Son lost it, but that, [[Phil 2:7|taking the form of a servant|forma servi accepta]], he appeared in lowliness. But then this sending would seem to refer to the time of the incarnation. Some grant this, and take *glory* in this place to mean the supremacy of the monarchy gained by the Romans, especially by Cæsar Augustus, under whom the world was enrolled[[Luke 2:1||]], and then Christ was born[[Luke 2:7||]]. But the words that follow do not seem to agree well enough. Others take this glory to mean the dominion of the Chaldeans: after the king of Babylon had gained it, the Son was sent by the Father with a spiritual sending to the nations that had robbed the Jews, namely to the Chaldeans, whom the Persians and Medes destroyed by the power of the Son of God. In which manner it is written of the Son of God in Wisdom: [[Wis 18:14|while all things were in quiet silence|Dum medium silentium tenerent omnia]], [[Wis 18:15|Thy Almighty word|omnipotens sermo tuus]], O Lord, [[Wis 18:15|leaped down from heaven from thy royal throne|de cœlo exsiliens, a regalibus sedibus venit]] [Denis quotes the form used in the Christmas liturgy: "While all things kept the midst of silence, thy almighty word, O Lord, leaping down from heaven, came from the royal throne"]. And there it speaks literally of the punishment of the Egyptians. Moreover, that it befits the Son to be sent spiritually, and not only by the incarnation and the nature he took, is taught well enough in the first book of the Sentences [of Peter Lombard, where the sending of the divine Persons is treated].

paras.t: Qui enim tetigerit, id est vexaverit, vos Judæos, qui estis populus meus, tanget pupillam oculi ejus, id est, se ipsum lædet : hoc est, tam diligenter vos custodiam, et injurias vobis illatas ulciscar, quod persequens vos sibi ipsi nocebit, ut is qui oculi sui pupillam molestat.
paras.en: [[2:8|for he that toucheth|Qui enim tetigerit]], that is, harasses, [[2:8|you|vos]] Jews, who are my people, [[2:8|toucheth the apple|tanget pupillam]] of his eye [Denis reads *oculi ejus*, "of his eye"; a footnote of the edition gives the other reading *mei*, "of my eye", as in the Douay-Rheims], that is, he will hurt himself: that is, I will guard you so carefully, and avenge the wrongs done you, that he who persecutes you will harm himself, like one who troubles the apple of his own eye.

paras.t: Quia ecce ego levo manum meam super eos, id est, potestate mea adversarios vestros dejiciam, et erunt prædæ his qui serviebant sibi. Hoc fuit impletum, quando Chaldæi victi fuerunt a Persis, et Persæ a Græcis, quia et aliqui reges Persarum adversabantur Judæis. Et cognoscetis per experientiam ultionis divinæ contra æmulos vestros, et per auxilium liberationis vestræ, quia Dominus exercituum misit me, modo jam declarato.
paras.en: [[2:9|For behold, I lift up my hand upon them|Quia ecce ego levo manum meam super eos]], that is, by my power I will cast down your adversaries, [[2:9|and they shall be a prey to those that served them|et erunt prædæ his qui serviebant sibi]]. This was fulfilled when the Chaldeans were conquered by the Persians, and the Persians by the Greeks, since some kings of the Persians also opposed the Jews. [[2:9|and you shall know|Et cognoscetis]] by experience of the divine vengeance against your foes, and by the help of your deliverance, [[2:9|that the Lord of hosts sent me|quia Dominus exercituum misit me]], in the manner already explained.

paras.t: Itaque pro tantis beneficiis invitatur populus Dei ad spiritualem lætitiam et gratiarum actionem : Lauda Deum, et lætare in eo, filia Sion, id est, plebs Synagogæ, quia ecce ego Dominus Deus tuus venio per misericordiæ meæ effectum, et habitabo in medio tui, per gratiæ infusionem et beneficiorum largitionem, ait Dominus. Unde per Moysen loquitur : Ego sum qui habito in medio filiorum Israel.
paras.en: So for such great benefits the people of God is invited to spiritual joy and thanksgiving: [[2:10|Sing praise|Lauda]] to God, [[2:10|and rejoice|et lætare]] in him, [[2:10|O daughter of Sion|filia Sion]], that is, people of the Synagogue, [[2:10|for behold I|quia ecce ego]], the Lord thy God, [[2:10|come|venio]] by the working of my mercy, [[2:10|and I will dwell in the midst of thee|et habitabo in medio tui]], by the pouring in of grace and the bestowing of benefits, [[2:10|saith the Lord|ait Dominus]]. Hence he says through Moses: I am he [[Num 35:34|that dwell among the children of Israel|qui habito in medio filiorum Israel]].

paras.t: Et applicabuntur gentes multæ ad Dominum in die illa : id est, tempore illo multi convertentur ad Dominum, adhærentes ei fideliter. Nam et Judæi post reditum a Chaldæa, multos gentilium fecerunt proselytos. Et erunt mihi in populum, id est de numero electorum meorum, et scies quia Dominus exercituum misit me ad te, o populo meus, quia ex effectibus istis pensabitis adsistentiam præsentiæ meæ.
paras.en: [[2:11|And many nations shall be joined to the Lord in that day|Et applicabuntur gentes multæ ad Dominum in die illa]]: that is, at that time many will be converted to the Lord, cleaving to him faithfully. For the Jews too, after the return from Chaldæa, made many of the Gentiles proselytes. [[2:11|and they shall be my people|Et erunt mihi in populum]], that is, of the number of my elect, [[2:11|and thou shalt know that the Lord of hosts hath sent me to thee|et scies quia Dominus exercituum misit me ad te]], O my people, because from these effects you will judge of the help of my presence.

paras.t: Et possidebit Dominus Judam, id est populum Judæorum, partem suam, id est plebem præ ceteris gentibus divino cultui deputatam, atque ab aliis separatam et præelectam : propter quod in Deuteronomio habetur, Pars autem Domini populus ejus ; et in libro Esther. Ne despicias partem tuam ; in terra sanctificata, videlicet in terra promissionis, quæ terra sancta vocatur, quia ad Dei obsequium ab antiquo deputata, et propter sanctos qui in ea fuerunt. Et eliget adhuc Jerusalem : sicut expositum est paulo ante.
paras.en: [[2:12|And the Lord shall possess Juda|Et possidebit Dominus Judam]], that is, the people of the Jews, [[2:12|his portion|partem suam]], that is, the people set apart before the other nations for the worship of God, and separated from the others and chosen beforehand: wherefore it is said in Deuteronomy, [[Deut 32:9|But the Lord's portion is his people|Pars autem Domini populus ejus]]; and in the book of Esther, [[Esth 13:16|Despise not thy portion|Ne despicias partem tuam]]; [[2:12|in the sanctified land|in terra sanctificata]], namely in the land of promise, which is called the holy land because it was set apart of old for the service of God, and because of the saints who were in it. [[2:12|and he shall yet choose Jerusalem|Et eliget adhuc Jerusalem]]: as was expounded a little before.

paras.t: Sileat omnis caro a facie Domini, id est, divinam justitiam metuat omnis homo, nec impie aliquid proferat contra Deum ; quia consurrexit de habitaculo sancto suo, id est, hostes populi sui dejicere est paratus : ita quod quasi de cœlo consurgere videtur, quando in terra aliquid novi terribiliter operatur. Unde oramus in Psalmo : Exsurge, Domine, adjuva nos. De quo in Deuteronomio scribitur : Habitaculum ejus sursum, et subter brachia sempiterna.
paras.en: [[2:13|Let all flesh be silent at the presence of the Lord|Sileat omnis caro a facie Domini]], that is, let every man fear the justice of God, and utter nothing impious against God; [[2:13|for he is risen up out of his holy habitation|quia consurrexit de habitaculo sancto suo]], that is, he is ready to cast down the enemies of his people: so that he seems to rise up as it were from heaven when he works something new and terrible on earth. Hence we pray in the Psalm: [[Ps 43:26|Arise, O Lord, help us|Exsurge, Domine, adjuva nos]]. Of whom it is written in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 33:27|His dwelling is above, and underneath are the everlasting arms|Habitaculum ejus sursum, et subter brachia sempiterna]] [the margin gives Deut. xxxii, 27; the words are Deut. xxxiii, 27].

paras.t: Hanc litteralem expositionem inserui, sequendo S. Hieronymum, qui etiam hic alibique frequenter hujusmodi expositiones inducit, potius Judæorum dicta recitando, quam aliquid de proprio asserendo.
paras.en: I have put in this literal exposition following St. Jerome, who here and elsewhere often brings in expositions of this kind, reciting the sayings of the Jews rather than asserting anything of his own.

paras.t: Præterea quibusdam expositio ista non placet, sed totum capitulum istud ab illo loco, Ecce angelus qui loquebatur in me, egrediebatur, etc., exponunt ad litteram de Christo et Ecclesia pro tempore gratiæ. Itaque quod dicitur, Absque muro habitabitur Jerusalem, exponunt sic : id est, Ecclesia in divina protectione confidit, non in muris et fortalitiis. Sed huic sensui non concordat quod subditur, præ multitudine hominum et jumentorum : ex quo insinuatur, quod multitudo hominum et jumentorum sit causa habitandi sine muris. Per homines autem intelligunt sapientes ac litteratos ; per jumenta, idiotas et simplices. Dicunt insuper, quod Jerusalem per Esdram et Nehemiam reædificata, semper fuit in timore inimicorum et subjectione extraneorum, usque ad ejus destructionem per Romanos. Cui repugnat illud libri primi Machabæorum : Et siluit terra Juda omnibus diebus Simonis ; et dilatavit fines gentis suæ, et obtinuit regionem. Et unusquisque colebat terram suam cum pace ; seniores in plateis sedebant omnes, et de bonis terræ tractabant, et juvenes induebant se gloriam. Civitatibus tribuebat alimonias, quoadusque nominatum est nomen gloriæ ejus usque ad extremum terræ ; fecit pacem super terram, et lætatus est Israel lætitia magna. Et sedit unusquisque sub vite sua, et sub ficulnea sua, nec erat qui eos terreret ; defecit impugnans eos super terram, reges contriti sunt in illis diebus. Præterea in libro Judith legitur : In omni spatio vitæ ejus, non fuit qui perturbaret Israel, et post mortem ejus annis multis.
paras.en: Further, some do not like this exposition, but expound the whole of this chapter, from the place [[2:3|And behold the angel that spoke in me went forth|Ecce angelus qui loquebatur in me, egrediebatur]], etc., literally of Christ and the Church in the time of grace. So what is said, [[2:4|Jerusalem shall be inhabited without walls|Absque muro habitabitur Jerusalem]], they expound thus: that is, the Church trusts in God's protection, not in walls and fortresses. But with this sense what follows does not agree, [[2:4|by reason of the multitude of men, and of the beasts|præ multitudine hominum et jumentorum]]: from which it is suggested that the multitude of men and beasts is the cause of dwelling without walls. By *men* they understand the wise and learned; by *beasts*, the unlettered and simple. They say besides that Jerusalem, rebuilt by Esdras and Nehemias, was always in fear of enemies and in subjection to foreigners, until its destruction by the Romans. Against which stands that passage of the first book of Machabees: [[1 Mach 14:4|And all the land of Juda was at rest all the days of Simon|Et siluit terra Juda omnibus diebus Simonis]]; [[1 Mach 14:6|And he enlarged the bounds of his nation, and made himself master of the country|et dilatavit fines gentis suæ, et obtinuit regionem]]. [[1 Mach 14:8|And every man tilled his land with peace|Et unusquisque colebat terram suam cum pace]]; [[1 Mach 14:9|The ancient men sat all in the streets, and treated together of the good things of the land, and the young men put on them glory|seniores in plateis sedebant omnes, et de bonis terræ tractabant, et juvenes induebant se gloriam]]. [[1 Mach 14:10|And he provided victuals for the cities|Civitatibus tribuebat alimonias]], [[1 Mach 14:10|so that the fame of his glory was renowned even to the end of the earth|quoadusque nominatum est nomen gloriæ ejus usque ad extremum terræ]]; [[1 Mach 14:11|He made peace in the land, and Israel rejoiced with great joy|fecit pacem super terram, et lætatus est Israel lætitia magna]]. [[1 Mach 14:12|And every man sat under his vine, and under his fig tree: and there was none to make them afraid|Et sedit unusquisque sub vite sua, et sub ficulnea sua, nec erat qui eos terreret]]; [[1 Mach 14:13|There was none left in the land to fight against them: kings were discomfited in those days|defecit impugnans eos super terram, reges contriti sunt in illis diebus]]. Further, in the book of Judith we read: [[Jdt 16:30|all the time of her life there was none that troubled Israel, nor many years after her death|In omni spatio vitæ ejus, non fuit qui perturbaret Israel, et post mortem ejus annis multis]].

paras.t: Quæ autem sequuntur, ita exponunt : O, o, o, fugite de terra aquilonis. O homines universi, et Christifideles, recedite de potestate diaboli, qui dixit : Sedebo in lateribus aquilonis. Quoniam in quatuor ventos cœli dispersi vos, id est, per varios errores ubique dispergi permisi ante Christi adventum, et ex quatuor ventis colligam vos sub ecclesiastica unitate per fidem et spem.
paras.en: What follows they expound thus: [[2:6|O, O flee ye out of the land of the north|O, o, o, fugite de terra aquilonis]]. O all men, and you faithful of Christ, withdraw from the power of the devil, who said: [[Is 14:13|I will sit|Sedebo]] [[Is 14:13|in the sides of the north|in lateribus aquilonis]]. [[2:6|for I have scattered you into the four winds of heaven|Quoniam in quatuor ventos cœli dispersi vos]], that is, I allowed you to be scattered everywhere through various errors before the coming of Christ, and from the four winds I will gather you into the unity of the Church through faith and hope.

paras.t: O Sion, fuge, id est, Ecclesia, de potestate diaboli te abstrahe, quæ habitas apud filiam Babylonis, id est cultum idololatriæ, et in vitiorum confusione. Non enim, ut dicunt, per filiam Babylonis potest hoc loco intelligi terra vel civitas Babylonis, quoniam ante hujus prophetiæ impletionem, fuit per Cyrum destructa, Judæi quoque fuerunt remissi. Rursus terra quæ hic dicitur Babylonis, immediate jam dicta est terra aquilonis. Babylonia autem non est ad aquilonem respectu Judææ, sed magis ad orientem. Verum hæc faciliter solverentur. Quamvis enim civitas nomine Babylon fuit destructa, non tamen omnia loca habitabilia Babyloniæ. Judæorum quoque quamplurimi, præcipue indevoti, in Babylonia post Cyri licentiam remanserunt, amore rerum quas ibi possidebant, itemque uxorum quas illic acceperant. Postremo, Hieronymus hic dicit, quod Assyrii et Babylonii habitabant in terra aquilonis, probatque hoc ex Jeremia.
paras.en: [[2:7|O Sion, flee|O Sion, fuge]], that is, O Church, draw thyself away from the power of the devil, [[2:7|thou that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon|quæ habitas apud filiam Babylonis]], that is, with the worship of idols, and in the confusion of vices. For, as they say, by the daughter of Babylon cannot be understood in this place the land or city of Babylon, since before the fulfilment of this prophecy it had been destroyed by Cyrus, and the Jews too had been sent back. Again, the land here called Babylon's has just been called the land of the north; but Babylonia is not to the north with respect to Judæa, but rather to the east. But these objections would easily be answered. For although the city called Babylon had been destroyed, not all the inhabitable places of Babylonia had been. And very many of the Jews, especially the undevout, stayed in Babylonia after Cyrus's leave, for love of the goods they possessed there, and likewise of the wives they had taken there. Lastly, Jerome says here that the Assyrians and Babylonians dwelt in the land of the north, and proves it from Jeremias[[Jer 1:13||]][[Jer 1:14||]][[Jer 1:15||]].

paras.t: Hæc dicit Dominus : Post gloriam monarchiæ a Romanis adeptæ, misit me unicum Filium suum Deus per incarnationis mysterium, ad gentes quæ spoliaverunt vos, id est ad infideles Judæos, qui primitivam Ecclesiam graviter afflixerunt, quibus tamen Christus prædicavit.
paras.en: [[2:8|thus saith the Lord|Hæc dicit Dominus]]: [[2:8|After the glory|Post gloriam]] of the monarchy gained by the Romans, God [[2:8|hath sent me|misit me]], his only Son, by the mystery of the incarnation, [[2:8|to the nations that have robbed you|ad gentes quæ spoliaverunt vos]], that is, to the unbelieving Jews, who sorely afflicted the early Church, and to whom Christ nevertheless preached.

paras.t: Ecce ego levo manum meam super eos, scilicet Ecclesiæ persecutores, et erunt prædæ his qui serviebant sibi. Hoc dicitur, quia Romani et alii multi Ecclesiam persequentes, tandem ad fidem conversi sunt, et servierunt Ecclesiæ. Et cognoscetis, o Christifideles, quia Dominus exercituum, scilicet Deus Pater, misit me ad te, o Ecclesia, per incarnationem pro tua salute.
paras.en: [[2:9|behold, I lift up my hand upon them|Ecce ego levo manum meam super eos]], namely the persecutors of the Church, [[2:9|and they shall be a prey to those that served them|et erunt prædæ his qui serviebant sibi]]. This is said because the Romans and many others who persecuted the Church were at length converted to the faith and served the Church. [[2:9|and you shall know|Et cognoscetis]], O faithful of Christ, [[2:9|that the Lord of hosts|quia Dominus exercituum]], namely God the Father, [[2:9|sent me|misit me]] to thee, O Church, by the incarnation, for thy salvation.

paras.t: Lauda et lætare, filia Sion, quia ecce venio, humanam naturam hypostatice assumendo, et habitabo in medio tui, ait Dominus. Christus enim homo factus, in terris est visus, et cum hominibus conversatus, juxta illud Joannis : Verbum caro factum est, et habitavit in nobis.
paras.en: [[2:10|Sing praise, and rejoice, O daughter of Sion|Lauda et lætare, filia Sion]], [[2:10|for behold I come|quia ecce venio]], by taking human nature hypostatically [that is, uniting it to himself in the one Person of the Word], [[2:10|and I will dwell in the midst of thee: saith the Lord|et habitabo in medio tui, ait Dominus]]. For Christ, made man, [[Bar 3:38|was seen upon earth, and conversed with men|in terris est visus, et cum hominibus conversatus]], according to that saying of John: [[John 1:14|the Word was made flesh and dwelt among us|Verbum caro factum est, et habitavit in nobis]].

paras.t: Et applicabuntur gentes multæ ad Dominum in die illa : id est, tempore gratiæ multi gentilium, imo et Judaicæ gentis, convertentur ad Christum. Quod constat impletum a tempore prædicationis Apostolorum, sicut prædixit Psalmista : Reminiscentur et convertentur ad Dominum universi fines terræ.
paras.en: [[2:11|And many nations shall be joined to the Lord in that day|Et applicabuntur gentes multæ ad Dominum in die illa]]: that is, in the time of grace many of the Gentiles, and indeed of the Jewish nation too, will be converted to Christ. This is plainly fulfilled from the time of the Apostles' preaching, as the Psalmist foretold: [[Ps 21:28|All the ends of the earth shall remember, and shall be converted to the Lord|Reminiscentur et convertentur ad Dominum universi fines terræ]].

paras.t: Denique ex præhabitis faciliter elucescit spiritualis hujus capituli intellectus : quem breviter tangam, ne nimia prolixitas fastidium pariat. Itaque per virum habentem in manu funiculum mensorum, intelligitur Christus omnium judex, in cujus potestate est æquitas atque scientia discernendi, mensurandi et judicandi virtutes et merita singulorum : ita quod judicandi auctoritas, scientia seu æquitas est iste funiculus. Hunc autem virum elevatis oculis mentis spiritualiter contemplatur Zacharias, id est quicumque fidelis Domini Dei jugiter reminiscens. Denique Christus vadit per providentiæ suæ extensionem, ut metiatur Jerusalem et Judæam, id est merita Christianorum : quatenus qua mensura mensi fuerimus, remetiatur nobis ; quanta sit latitudo ejus in caritate, an scilicet diligat etiam inimicos, et longitudo ejus in perseverantia. Altitudo autem est in contemplatione, et profunditas in humilitate.
paras.en: Lastly, from what has gone before, the spiritual understanding of this chapter shines out easily; I will touch on it briefly, lest too great length breed weariness. So by the man [[2:1|with a measuring line in his hand|habentem in manu funiculum mensorum]] is understood Christ, the judge of all, in whose power is the equity and the knowledge to discern, measure and judge the virtues and merits of each: so that this line is the authority, knowledge or equity of judging. And this man Zacharias contemplates spiritually with the eyes of the mind lifted up: that is, every faithful soul that is mindful always of the Lord God [*Zacharias* is taken to mean "mindful of the Lord"]. Then Christ goes, by the reach of his providence, [[2:2|To measure Jerusalem|ut metiatur Jerusalem]] and Judæa, that is, the merits of Christians: so that with what measure we have measured, it may be measured to us again[[Matt 7:2||]]; [[2:2|how great is the breadth thereof|quanta sit latitudo ejus]] in charity, namely whether it loves even its enemies, [[2:2|and how great the length thereof|et longitudo ejus]] in perseverance. The height, then, is in contemplation, and the depth in humility.

paras.t: Quod insuper Christus sit Ecclesiæ murus, testatur Isaias, dicendo : Urbs fortitudinis nostræ Sion, Salvator ponetur in ea murus et antemurale ; item Psalmista : Dominus in circuitu populi sui, ex hoc nunc et usque in sæculum.
paras.en: Moreover, that Christ is the wall of the Church [as in v. 5, "a wall of fire round about"], Isaias testifies, saying: [[Is 26:1|Sion the city of our strength a saviour, a wall and a bulwark shall be set therein|Urbs fortitudinis nostræ Sion, Salvator ponetur in ea murus et antemurale]]; and likewise the Psalmist: [[Ps 124:2|the Lord is round about his people from henceforth now and for ever|Dominus in circuitu populi sui, ex hoc nunc et usque in sæculum]].

paras.t: Fugite de terra aquilonis, id est frigore sæcularis conversationis, et hominibus in quibus amor Christi refriguit. Nomine quippe aquilonis, unde frigidissimus oritur ventus, isti signantur. Quoniam in quatuor ventos cœli dispersi vos. Ubique enim boni et impii sunt commixti. Unde mente fugiendum est, si corporaliter fugere non suppetit : hoc est non communicare, nec conformari affectibus atque operibus amatorum sæculi hujus.
paras.en: [[2:6|flee ye out of the land of the north|Fugite de terra aquilonis]], that is, from the coldness of worldly living, and from men in whom the love of Christ has grown cold[[Matt 24:12||]]. For by the name of the north, whence the coldest wind arises, these are signified. [[2:6|for I have scattered you into the four winds of heaven|Quoniam in quatuor ventos cœli dispersi vos]]. For everywhere the good and the wicked are mingled together. Hence one must flee in mind, if it is not possible to flee in body: that is, not to have fellowship with, nor be conformed to, the affections and works of the lovers of this world.

paras.t: O Sion, id est, anima fidelis, fuge a malo : juxta quod scriptum est in Ecclesiastico, Quasi a facie colubri fuge peccatum ; quæ habitas apud filiam Babylonis, id est eam quæ vitiorum inordinatione confusa est et distorta, non quærens nisi quæ mundi sunt et commoda carnis, ne cum perversa pervertaris. Qui enim tetigerit picem, inquinatur. Et mala societas summe vitanda est, quum sit utique summe nociva. Ideo dicit Apostolus : Exite de medio eorum, et immundum ne tetigeritis ; Moyses quoque, Recedite, inquit, a tabernaculis hominum impiorum.
paras.en: [[2:7|O Sion|O Sion]], that is, faithful soul, [[2:7|flee|fuge]] from evil: according to what is written in Ecclesiasticus, [[Ecclus 21:2|Flee from sins as from the face of a serpent|Quasi a facie colubri fuge peccatum]]; [[2:7|thou that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon|quæ habitas apud filiam Babylonis]], that is, with her who is confounded and distorted by the disorder of vices, seeking nothing but the things of the world and the comforts of the flesh, lest with the perverse thou be perverted[[Ps 17:27||]]. For [[Ecclus 13:1|He that toucheth pitch, shall be defiled|Qui enim tetigerit picem, inquinatur]]. And bad company is above all to be shunned, since it is above all harmful. Therefore the Apostle says: [[2 Cor 6:17|Go out from among them|Exite de medio eorum]], [[2 Cor 6:17|and touch not the unclean thing|et immundum ne tetigeritis]]; and Moses too: [[Num 16:26|Depart|Recedite]], he says, [[Num 16:26|from the tents of these wicked men|a tabernaculis hominum impiorum]].

paras.t: Qui tetigerit vos, tanget pupillam oculi mei. In hoc manifestatur qualiter Deus Christus suos amet et protegat, eorumque ulciscatur injurias. Propter quod ait ad Paulum : Quid me persequeris? Et rursus in Evangelio : Quod uni ex minimis meis fecistis, mihi fecistis. Insuper persecutores bonorum divinitus opprimentur, electorumque pedibus saltem in die judicii subjicientur.
paras.en: [[2:8|he that toucheth you, toucheth the apple of my eye|Qui tetigerit vos, tanget pupillam oculi mei]]. In this is shown how God, Christ, loves and protects his own, and avenges the wrongs done them. Wherefore he says to Paul: [[Acts 9:4|why persecutest thou me?|Quid me persequeris?]] And again in the Gospel: [[Matt 25:40|as long as you did it to one of these my least brethren, you did it to me|Quod uni ex minimis meis fecistis, mihi fecistis]]. Besides, the persecutors of the good will be crushed by God, and will be put under the feet of the elect, at least on the day of judgement.

paras.t: Lauda et lætare, filia Sion, id est, Ecclesia seu anima speculativa, quia venio et habitabo in medio tui. In cordibus enim devotis gratiose moratur, et in Ecclesia per sacramentalem præsentiam manere inæstimabili caritate dignatur. Hinc in Levitico Dominus loquitur : Ponam tabernaculum meum in medio vestrum, et non abjiciet vos anima mea ; et ambulabo inter vos, et ero vester Deus, vosque eritis mihi populus. Ecce quam incomprehensibilis est dignatio Dei superaltissimi ad nos miseros pauperrimosque vermiculos. Simus igitur grati caritati, pietati et beneficiis ejus ad nos, ipsum delectabiliter collaudando, laudabiliterque in ipso semper gaudendo, nec bonitatis ac gratiæ ejus ullatenus obliviscendo.
paras.en: [[2:10|Sing praise, and rejoice, O daughter of Sion|Lauda et lætare, filia Sion]], that is, O Church, or contemplative soul, for [[2:10|I come, and I will dwell in the midst of thee|venio et habitabo in medio tui]]. For he dwells graciously in devout hearts, and in the Church he deigns, with inestimable charity, to abide by his sacramental presence. Hence in Leviticus the Lord says: [[Lev 26:11|I will set my tabernacle in the midst of you: and my soul shall not cast you off|Ponam tabernaculum meum in medio vestrum, et non abjiciet vos anima mea]]; [[Lev 26:12|I will walk among you, and will be your God: and you shall be my people|et ambulabo inter vos, et ero vester Deus, vosque eritis mihi populus]]. See how beyond understanding is the condescension of the most high God towards us, wretched and most poor little worms. Let us then be grateful for his charity, his love and his benefits towards us, praising him with delight, ever rejoicing in him in a praiseworthy manner, and never in any way forgetting his goodness and grace.

3.title: Elucidatio capituli tertii: Et ostendit mihi Dominus Jesum sacerdotem magnum.
3.title_en: Explanation of the third chapter: And the Lord shewed me Jesus the high priest.

paras.t: Et ostendit mihi Dominus Jesum sacerdotem magnum stantem coram angelo Domini. Sicut refert Hieronymus, Judæi hunc locum ad litteram exponunt de Jesu filio Josedec sacerdote magno : et littera ad hoc satis aptatur. Sed quia inferius, quando de Jesu isto locutus est Zacharias, semper adjecit nomen patris ejus, hic autem simpliciter exprimit nomen ejus, idcirco quidam catholici putant hæc ad litteram de Jesu Christo Domino nostro prolata : quod difficile est tenere, sicut patebit.
paras.en: [[3:1|And the Lord shewed me Jesus the high priest standing before the angel of the Lord|Et ostendit mihi Dominus Jesum sacerdotem magnum stantem coram angelo Domini]]. As Jerome relates, the Jews expound this passage literally of Jesus the son of Josedec, the high priest; and the letter fits this well enough. But because further on, when Zacharias speaks of this Jesus, he always adds his father's name, whereas here he gives his name alone, some Catholics therefore think that these words were spoken literally of Jesus Christ our Lord: which is difficult to hold, as will become clear.

paras.t: Ostendente igitur Deo, vidit in spiritu Zacharias Jesum filium Josedec pontificem, qui cum Zorobabel præfuit populo, stantem coram angelo Dei, illo videlicet qui stetit inter myrteta, et præfuit Synagogæ, utpote Michaele, sicut communiter dicitur. Et Satan, id est adversarius nostræ salutis diabolus, stabat a dextris ejus, ut adversaretur ei, id est, eum accusaret, præsertim de acceptione uxorum alienigenarum sive gentilium : quia ut Esdras narrat, Judæi et sacerdotes atque Levitæ de Babylone reversi, graviter peccaverunt alienigenas contra legem ducendo uxores. Fuitque in hoc etiam Jesus iste culpabilis, vel quia et ipse talem accepit uxorem, ut affirmat Hieronymus, vel quoniam subditos suos et proprios filios in hoc reos, non satis redarguit, sicut primo Regum Heli sacerdos divinitus increpatur, quod filios suos condigne non arguit. Porro dictum Hieronymi ex hoc posset fulciri, quod in Esdra habetur quemadmodum manus principum et magistratuum fuit in transgressione hac prima. In eodem libro legitur : Inventi sunt de filiis sacerdotum, qui duxerunt uxores alienigenas : de filiis Josue, filii Josedec, et fratres ejus, etc. Unde, secundum Hieronymum, diabolus stat a dextris Jesu istius, quoniam vera fuit accusatio ejus.
paras.en: So, God showing him, Zacharias saw in the spirit Jesus the son of Josedec, the high priest, who with Zorobabel governed the people, [[3:1|standing before the angel|stantem coram angelo]] of God: that is, the one who stood among the myrtle trees[[Zach 1:8||]] and presided over the Synagogue, namely Michael, as is commonly said. And [[3:1|Satan|Satan]], that is, the devil, the adversary of our salvation, [[3:1|stood on his right hand to be his adversary|stabat a dextris ejus, ut adversaretur ei]], that is, to accuse him, above all of taking foreign or heathen wives: for, as Esdras relates, the Jews, and the priests and Levites, having returned from Babylon, sinned grievously by marrying foreign wives against the law[[1 Esd 9:1||]][[1 Esd 9:2||]]. And this Jesus too was at fault in this[[1 Esd 10:18||]], either because he himself also took such a wife, as Jerome asserts, or because he did not sufficiently rebuke his subjects and his own sons who were guilty in this, as in the first book of Kings the priest Heli is rebuked by God for not reproving his sons as they deserved[[1 Kings 2:29||]] [the margin gives 1 Reg. ii, 20; God's rebuke of Heli is at 1 Kings 2:29, and again at 3:13]. Moreover, Jerome's statement could be supported by this, that in Esdras we find how [[1 Esd 9:2|the hand of the princes and magistrates hath been first in this transgression|manus principum et magistratuum fuit in transgressione hac prima]]. In the same book we read: [[1 Esd 10:18|And there were found among the sons of the priests that had taken strange wives: Of the sons of Josue the son of Josedec, and his brethren|Inventi sunt de filiis sacerdotum, qui duxerunt uxores alienigenas : de filiis Josue, filii Josedec, et fratres ejus]], etc. Hence, according to Jerome, the devil stands at the right hand of this Jesus, because his accusation was true.

paras.t: Et dixit Dominus ad Satan : Increpet Dominus in te, Satan, id est, accusatio tua redarguatur, et tu reprobus convincaris, qui invidiose accusas; et increpet Dominus in te, id est, increpationem suam contra te dirigat, qui elegit Jerusalem, ut cultus Dei in ea recuperetur. Denique in modo hujus locutionis designatur implicite trinitas Personarum in simplici Deo. Ter enim ponitur, Dominus; et in Hebræo exprimitur nomen tetragrammaton, quod soli vero convenit Deo. Loquitur namque Dominus de Domino, quasi una Persona de alia, seu Pater de Filio. Huic etiam modo loquendi consonat illud in Genesi : Pluit Dominus super Sodomam et Gomorrham ignem et sulfur a Domino. Causa insuper increpationis Satan a Domino, subditur : Numquid non iste, videlicet Jesus quem accusas, torris est erutus de igne, id est similis titioni semiusto ? quia de Babylonica captivitate, quasi de igne tribulationis evasit, et tu ultra hoc quæris eum obruere, et quasi totum comburere.
paras.en: [[3:2|And the Lord said to Satan: The Lord rebuke thee, O Satan|Et dixit Dominus ad Satan : Increpet Dominus in te, Satan]], that is, let thy accusation be refuted, and mayest thou be convicted as reprobate, thou who accusest out of envy; and [[3:2|the Lord rebuke thee|increpet Dominus in te]], that is, may he direct his rebuke against thee, he [[3:2|that chose Jerusalem|qui elegit Jerusalem]], that the worship of God might be restored in it. Moreover, in the manner of this utterance the trinity of Persons in the simple God is implicitly signified. For "Lord" is set down three times; and in the Hebrew the name tetragrammaton is expressed [that is, the four-lettered proper name of God], which befits the true God alone. For the Lord speaks of the Lord, as one Person of another, or the Father of the Son. With this manner of speaking also accords that in Genesis: [[Gen 19:24|the Lord rained upon Sodom and Gomorrha brimstone and fire from the Lord|Pluit Dominus super Sodomam et Gomorrham ignem et sulfur a Domino]]. Then the reason for the Lord's rebuke of Satan is added: [[3:2|Is not this|Numquid non iste]], namely Jesus whom thou accusest, [[3:2|a brand plucked out of the fire|torris est erutus de igne]], that is, like a half-burnt firebrand? For he escaped from the Babylonian captivity as from the fire of tribulation, and thou seekest beyond this to overwhelm him and, as it were, to burn him up altogether.

paras.t: Et Jesus erat indutus vestibus sordidis, id est, anima ejus vitio negligentiæ et peccati præfati fuit operta et maculata, et ipse squalore captivitatis erat confectus. Sicut enim virtutes et opera bona sunt splendida animæ vestimenta, sic passiones et vitia vestes sunt sordidæ. Unde in Psalmo cantatur : Induantur, qui detrahunt mihi, pudore. Et stabat ante faciem angeli principis Synagogæ.
paras.en: [[3:3|And Jesus was clothed with filthy garments|Et Jesus erat indutus vestibus sordidis]], that is, his soul was covered and stained with the vice of negligence and of the sin mentioned above, and he himself was worn down by the squalor of the captivity. For as virtues and good works are the splendid garments of the soul, so passions and vices are filthy clothes. Hence it is sung in the Psalm: [[Ps 108:29|Let them that detract me be clothed with shame|Induantur, qui detrahunt mihi, pudore]]. [[3:3|And he stood before the face of the angel|Et stabat ante faciem angeli]], the prince of the Synagogue.

paras.t: Qui respondit, et ait ad eos qui stabant coram se, id est ad angelos inferiores præsentes, dicens : Auferte vestimenta sordida ab eo, id est, a peccatis eum purgate instrumentaliter, disponendo eum ad pœnitentiam veram seu pleniorem. Deus enim solus remittit et aufert peccata principaliter; angeli vero purgando, hortando, illuminando disponunt ad hoc. Et dixit ad eum, id est angelus superior ad Jesum : Ecce abstuli a te iniquitatem tuam, quia et angelis id commisi, et principalius eis hoc feci; et indui te mutatoriis, id est ornatu gratiæ ac virtutum; vel, secundum Hebræos, Israelitidem tibi conjugem copulavi.
paras.en: [[3:4|Who answered, and said to them that stood before him|Qui respondit, et ait ad eos qui stabant coram se]], that is, to the lower angels who were present, [[3:4|saying: Take away the filthy garments from him|dicens : Auferte vestimenta sordida ab eo]], that is, cleanse him from his sins as instruments [that is, as God's instruments, God himself being the principal cause], by disposing him to a true or a fuller penance. For God alone remits and takes away sins as their principal cause; but the angels dispose to this by cleansing, exhorting and enlightening. [[3:4|And he said to him|Et dixit ad eum]], that is, the higher angel to Jesus: [[3:4|Behold I have taken away thy iniquity|Ecce abstuli a te iniquitatem tuam]], because I both committed this to the angels and did it myself more principally than they; [[3:4|and have clothed thee with change of garments|et indui te mutatoriis]], that is, with the adornment of grace and of the virtues; or, according to the Hebrews, I have joined thee to an Israelite wife.

paras.t: Et dixit angelus iste superior inferioribus angelis : Ponite cidarim mundam, id est mitram episcopalem, super caput ejus. Et posuerunt cidarim mundam super caput ejus, id est, pontificali honore atque officio dignum eum fecerunt, vel ostenderunt, et induerunt eum vestibus ad summum sacerdotem spectantibus. Totum istud fiebat coram Zacharia propheta spirituali repræsentatione, non vana, sed aliquid veraciter significans.
paras.en: [[3:5|And he said|Et dixit]], this higher angel, to the lower angels: [[3:5|Put a clean mitre|Ponite cidarim mundam]], that is, a bishop's mitre, [[3:5|upon his head|super caput ejus]]. [[3:5|And they put a clean mitre upon his head|Et posuerunt cidarim mundam super caput ejus]], that is, they made him, or showed him to be, worthy of the pontifical honour and office, [[3:5|and clothed him with garments|et induerunt eum vestibus]] belonging to the high priest. All this was done before Zacharias the prophet by a spiritual representation: not an empty one, but one truly signifying something.

paras.t: Et angelus Domini iste superior stabat; et contestabatur angelus Domini Jesum, dicens : Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum : Si in viis meis ambulaveris, legis præcepta implendo, et custodiam meam custodieris, id est, cultum et cæremonias templi, tuumque officium reverenter ac diligenter impleveris ; tu quoque judicabis domum meam, id est populum Synagogæ, præsertim in spiritualibus causis, et custodies atria mea, id est, pontifex perseverabis; et dabo tibi ambulantes, id est tecum manentes teque custodientes, de his qui nunc hic adsistunt, id est, de numero angelorum istorum quosdam ad tui et tuorum custodiam deputabo, ne a Satana convincaris.
paras.en: [[3:5|And the angel of the Lord|Et angelus Domini]], this higher one, [[3:5|stood|stabat]]; [[3:6|and the angel of the Lord protested to Jesus, saying|et contestabatur angelus Domini Jesum, dicens]]: [[3:7|Thus saith the Lord of hosts|Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum]]: [[3:7|If thou wilt walk in my ways|Si in viis meis ambulaveris]], by fulfilling the precepts of the law, [[3:7|and keep my charge|et custodiam meam custodieris]], that is, if thou carry out the worship and ceremonies of the temple, and thine own office, reverently and diligently; [[3:7|thou also shalt judge my house|tu quoque judicabis domum meam]], that is, the people of the Synagogue, especially in spiritual causes, [[3:7|and shalt keep my courts|et custodies atria mea]], that is, thou shalt continue as high priest; [[3:7|and I will give thee|et dabo tibi]] some [[3:7|to walk with thee|ambulantes]], that is, to stay with thee and guard thee, [[3:7|of them that are now present here|de his qui nunc hic adsistunt]], that is, I will appoint some of the number of these angels to guard thee and thine, lest thou be convicted by Satan.

paras.t: Consequenter Dominus populum Synagogæ consolatur, prænuntiando Christi adventum. Audi, Jesu fili Josedec, sacerdos magne, tu et amici tui, qui habitant coram te, id est, qui tibi in cultu divino concordes sunt, tibique subditi et circa te commorantes, quia viri, id est prædicti tui amici, portendentes sunt, id est visum spiritualem procul in posterum extendentes, de Christi adventu vaticinando, vel eum præstolando. Isti viri fuerunt Prophetæ tempore Jesu hujus prophetantes, scilicet Aggæus, Zacharias, Malachias, ac ceteri justi Christum cordialiter advenire optantes. Vel, Viri portendentes sunt, id est portentum dantes, sicut ad Ezechielem Dominus ait, Portentum te dedi domui Israel; vel quia in signum sunt positi futurorum. Ecce enim ego adducam servum meum Orientem, id est Christum, qui est splendor gloriæ, et candor lucis æternæ : de quo in Evangelio dicitur, Visitavit nos Oriens ex altò. Ipse namque est oriens ille fons universæ lucis, nascens ex æterno supersplendidissimo Patre, quemadmodum in Ecclesiastico fatetur : Ego ex ore Altissimi prodivi, primogenita ante omnem creaturam; ego feci in cœlis ut oriretur lumen indeficiens.
paras.en: Next the Lord consoles the people of the Synagogue by foretelling the coming of Christ. [[3:8|Hear, O Jesus|Audi, Jesu]], son of Josedec, [[3:8|thou high priest, thou and thy friends that dwell before thee|sacerdos magne, tu et amici tui, qui habitant coram te]], that is, who are of one mind with thee in the worship of God, subject to thee and dwelling about thee; for the [[3:8|men|viri]], that is, thy friends just named, [[3:8|are portending|portendentes sunt]], that is, they reach out their spiritual sight far into what is to come, by prophesying the coming of Christ or by waiting for him. These men were the Prophets who prophesied in the time of this Jesus, namely Aggeus, Zacharias and Malachias, and the other just men who longed with all their hearts for Christ to come. Or, [[3:8|they are portending men|Viri portendentes sunt]], that is, they give a portent [portentum, a sign of things to come: the noun behind portendentes], as the Lord says to Ezechiel: [[Ezech 12:6|I have set thee for a sign of things to come to the house of Israel|Portentum te dedi domui Israel]]; or because they are set for a sign of things to come. [[3:8|For behold, I WILL BRING MY SERVANT THE ORIENT|Ecce enim ego adducam servum meum Orientem]], that is, Christ, who is [[Heb 1:3|the brightness of his glory|splendor gloriæ]], and [[Wis 7:26|the brightness of eternal light|candor lucis æternæ]]: of whom it is said in the Gospel: [[Luke 1:78|the Orient from on high hath visited us|Visitavit nos Oriens ex altò]]. For he is that rising Orient [oriens: the dawn, the rising of the sun], the fount of all light, born of the eternal and supremely resplendent Father, as he confesses in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 24:5|I came out of the mouth of the most High, the firstborn before all creatures|Ego ex ore Altissimi prodivi, primogenita ante omnem creaturam]]; [[Ecclus 24:6|I made that in the heavens there should rise light that never faileth|ego feci in cœlis ut oriretur lumen indeficiens]].

paras.t: Quia ecce lapis quem dedi coram Jesu, id est Christus seu Oriens, quem per fidem et Prophetarum oracula manifestavi huic Jesu Josedec esse venturum : qui est lapis angularis, faciens utraque unum, lapis fortissimus qui omnia regna terræ contrivit, et apud Danielem de monte sine manibus abscissus describitur. De quo in Isaia loquitur Deus : Ecce ego mittam in fundamentis Sion lapidem angularem, probatum, pretiosum, in fundamento fundatum. Quem vidit filius Josedec, sicut de Abraham ait Salvator Judæis : Abraham pater vester exsultavit, ut videret diem meum; vidit, et gavisus est. Super lapidem unum, id est in Christo, in quo sunt duæ naturæ, sed una hypostasis, septem oculi sunt, id est septem dona Spiritus Sancti, quibus anima limpide videt quid scire et agere debeat. Et quamvis tria istorum donorum, videlicet fortitudo, pietas, timor, ad voluntatem subjective pertineant, oculi tamen dicuntur, quia clarificant animam. Fueruntque dona ista in anima Christi perfectissime atque plenissime, præsertim quantum ad actus quos habent in patria. Propter quod Isaias : Requiescet, inquit, super eum spiritus sapientiæ et intellectus, spiritus consilii et fortitudinis, spiritus scientiæ et pietatis, et replebit eum spiritus timoris Domini.
paras.en: [[3:9|For behold the stone that I have laid before Jesus|Quia ecce lapis quem dedi coram Jesu]], that is, Christ, or the Orient, whom through faith and the oracles of the Prophets I made known to this Jesus, son of Josedec, as one to come: who is [[Eph 2:20|the chief corner stone|lapis angularis]], [[Eph 2:14|who hath made both one|faciens utraque unum]], the mightiest stone, which broke in pieces all the kingdoms of the earth[[Dan 2:44||]], and is described in Daniel as [[Dan 2:34|cut out of a mountain without hands|de monte sine manibus abscissus]][[Dan 2:45||]]. Of him God speaks in Isaias: [[Is 28:16|Behold I will lay a stone in the foundations of Sion, a tried stone, a corner stone, a precious stone, founded in the foundation|Ecce ego mittam in fundamentis Sion lapidem angularem, probatum, pretiosum, in fundamento fundatum]]. Him the son of Josedec saw, as the Saviour says to the Jews of Abraham: [[John 8:56|Abraham your father rejoiced that he might see my day: he saw it and was glad|Abraham pater vester exsultavit, ut videret diem meum; vidit, et gavisus est]]. [[3:9|Upon one stone|Super lapidem unum]], that is, in Christ, in whom there are two natures but one hypostasis [that is, one person], [[3:9|there are seven eyes|septem oculi sunt]], that is, the seven gifts of the Holy Ghost, by which the soul sees clearly what it ought to know and to do. And although three of these gifts, namely fortitude, godliness and fear, belong to the will as their subject [that is, they reside in the will, not in the intellect], they are still called eyes, because they give light to the soul. And these gifts were in the soul of Christ most perfectly and most fully, especially as regards the acts which they have in the fatherland [that is, in heaven]. For which reason Isaias: There [[Is 11:2|shall rest|Requiescet]], he says, [[Is 11:2|upon him: the spirit of wisdom, and of understanding, the spirit of counsel, and of fortitude, the spirit of knowledge, and of godliness|super eum spiritus sapientiæ et intellectus, spiritus consilii et fortitudinis, spiritus scientiæ et pietatis]], [[Is 11:3|and he shall be filled with the spirit of the fear of the Lord|et replebit eum spiritus timoris Domini]].

paras.t: Præterea, quod loco præsenti per Orientem Christus, non Zorobabel vel alius intelligatur secundum Lyram, ex translatione Chaldaica authentica apud Judæos ostenditur, ubi sic legitur : Ecce ego adducam servum meum Messiam, et revelabitur.
paras.en: Moreover, that in the present passage Christ is meant by [[3:8|the Orient|Orientem]], and not Zorobabel or anyone else, is shown, according to Lyra, from the Chaldee translation, which is authoritative among the Jews, where it reads thus: Behold, I will bring my servant the Messias, and he shall be revealed.

paras.t: Præterea, quidam per septem oculos intelligunt universitatem angelicorum spirituum, qui sunt oculi intellectuales, ad Christi cultum obsequiumque parati. Nempe quod septenario universitas designetur, innuitur in Tobiæ libro, ubi Raphael ait : Ego sum unus ex septem qui adstamus ante Deum. Et in Apocalypsi inducitur : A septem spiritibus qui in conspectu throni ejus sunt.
paras.en: Moreover, some understand by the [[3:9|seven eyes|septem oculos]] the whole company of the angelic spirits, who are intellectual eyes, ready for the worship and service of Christ. For that the whole is signified by the number seven is hinted in the book of Tobias, where Raphael says: [[Tob 12:15|I am|Ego sum]] [[Tob 12:15|one of the seven, who stand before the Lord|unus ex septem qui adstamus ante Deum]]. And in the Apocalypse we have: [[Apoc 1:4|from the seven spirits which are before his throne|A septem spiritibus qui in conspectu throni ejus sunt]].

paras.t: Ecce ego cœlabo sculpturam ejus, ait Dominus exercituum: id est, corpus Christi in utero Virginis supernaturaliter formabo, et subito organizabo ; vel, secundum Hieronymum, corpus ejus in passione flagellis, clavis, spinis ac lancea vulnerari ac perforari permittam. Unde Septuaginta transtulerunt, Ego fodiam foveam; et Christus ait in Psalmo, Foderunt manus meas et pedes meos. Et auferam iniquitatem terræ illius, id est totius mundi, vel Synagogæ, sive Ecclesiæ, in die una, puta in die dominicæ passionis. Christus namque quantum in se est, pro omnibus satisfecit : de quo dictum est, Ecce Agnus Dei qui tollit peccata mundi.
paras.en: [[3:9|Behold I will grave the graving thereof, saith the Lord of hosts|Ecce ego cœlabo sculpturam ejus, ait Dominus exercituum]]: that is, I will form the body of Christ in the Virgin's womb supernaturally, and give it its members in an instant; or, according to Jerome, I will permit his body in the passion to be wounded and pierced with scourges, nails, thorns and the lance. Hence the Septuagint translated: I will dig a pit; and Christ says in the Psalm: [[Ps 21:17|They have dug my hands and feet|Foderunt manus meas et pedes meos]]. [[3:9|And I will take away the iniquity of that land|Et auferam iniquitatem terræ illius]], that is, of the whole world, or of the Synagogue, or of the Church, [[3:9|in one day|in die una]], namely on the day of the Lord's passion. For Christ, as far as lay in him, made satisfaction for all: of whom it was said: [[John 1:29|Behold the Lamb of God|Ecce Agnus Dei]] [[John 1:29|who taketh away the sin of the world|qui tollit peccata mundi]].

paras.t: In die illa (de qua fertur in Psalmo, Hæc est dies quam fecit Dominus, exsultemus et lætemur in ea), hoc est statim post Christi passionem misso desuper Spiritu Sancto, dicit Dominus exercituum, vocabit vir amicum suum, id est, unus alium invitabit venire, subter vineam et subter ficum, id est ad Christi ovile et pascua ejus, ad dona et unitatem Ecclesiæ, ad spirituales consolationes atque divitias. Hoc maxime impleverunt Apostoli, aliique viri perfecti, dona gratiæ sibi collata in alios administrare fervide cupientes. Vel certe per istum modum loquendi in Scripturis veteris Testamenti frequentem, insinuatur abundantia divitiarum et pacis in populo Judæorum. Et sic fuit in Christi adventu. Judæi enim tunc in temporalium affluentia ac pace fuerunt, omnibus regnis imperatori Romano subjectis.
paras.en: [[3:10|In that day|In die illa]] (of which it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 117:24|This is the day which the Lord hath made: let us be glad and rejoice therein|Hæc est dies quam fecit Dominus, exsultemus et lætemur in ea]]), that is, straightway after Christ's passion, when the Holy Ghost had been sent from above, [[3:10|saith the Lord of hosts, every man shall call his friend|dicit Dominus exercituum, vocabit vir amicum suum]], that is, one will invite another to come, [[3:10|under the vine and under the fig tree|subter vineam et subter ficum]] [Denis reads vineam, "vineyard", where the Vulgate has vitem, "vine"], that is, to the fold of Christ and his pastures, to the gifts and the unity of the Church, to spiritual consolations and riches. This the Apostles above all fulfilled, and other perfect men, who fervently desired to dispense to others the gifts of grace bestowed on them. Or else, by this manner of speech, frequent in the Scriptures of the Old Testament, an abundance of riches and of peace in the Jewish people is signified. And so it was at the coming of Christ: for the Jews were then in plenty of temporal goods and at peace, all kingdoms being subject to the Roman emperor.

paras.t: Jam intuendum, qualiter omnia ista possint de Christo intelligi. Itaque quidam catholici ita exponunt : Et ostendit mihi Dominus Jesum sacerdotem magnum, id est Christum Salvatorem : de quo legitur in Psalmo, Tu es sacerdos in æternum; et ad Hebræos, Habentes pontificem magnum, qui penetravit cœlum, Jesum Filium Dei ; stantem coram angelo Domini, id est coram se ipso magni consilii Angelo : quia in quantum homo mortalis, propter nos infirmatus apparuit coram se ipso, ut Dei et hominum summo mediatore, imo et vero Deo. Et Satan stabat a dextris ejus, ut adversaretur ei. De hoc in Evangelio legitur, quemadmodum ductus est a Spiritu in desertum, ut tentaretur a diabolo. Passione quoque instante dixit : Venit princeps mundi hujus, et in me non habet quidquam. Ideo ad Hebræos dicit Apostolus : Tentatus est per omnia absque peccato.
paras.en: Now we must see how all these things can be understood of Christ. Some Catholics, then, expound it thus: [[3:1|And the Lord shewed me Jesus the high priest|Et ostendit mihi Dominus Jesum sacerdotem magnum]], that is, Christ the Saviour, of whom we read in the Psalm: [[Ps 109:4|Thou art a priest for ever|Tu es sacerdos in æternum]]; and in Hebrews: [[Heb 4:14|Having therefore a great high priest that hath passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God|Habentes pontificem magnum, qui penetravit cœlum, Jesum Filium Dei]]; [[3:1|standing before the angel of the Lord|stantem coram angelo Domini]], that is, before himself, the Angel of great counsel[[Is 9:6||]] [the margin gives Is. ix, 6, according to the Septuagint, which names him "Angel of great counsel"; the Douay-Rheims, following the Vulgate, does not have these words]: for in so far as he was mortal man, made weak for our sake, he appeared before himself, as before the supreme mediator of God and men, nay, before the true God. [[3:1|And Satan stood on his right hand to be his adversary|Et Satan stabat a dextris ejus, ut adversaretur ei]]. Of this we read in the Gospel how he [[Matt 4:1|was led by the spirit into the desert, to be tempted by the devil|ductus est a Spiritu in desertum, ut tentaretur a diabolo]]. And when his passion was at hand he said: [[John 14:30|The prince of this world: cometh: and in me he hath not any thing|Venit princeps mundi hujus, et in me non habet quidquam]]. Therefore the Apostle says in Hebrews: He was [[Heb 4:15|tempted in all things|Tentatus est per omnia]] [[Heb 4:15|without sin|absque peccato]].

paras.t: Et dixit Dominus Jesus ad Satan : Increpet Dominus in te. Hoc Christus dixit et fecit, dum tertia tentatione completa, respondit : Vade, Satana; scriptum est, Non tentabis Dominum Deum tuum. Christus enim se ipsum Dominum dixit, et ipse se ipsum ad increpationem Satanæ excitavit. Numquid non iste torris est erutus de igne? Hoc Christo rectissime convenit, cujus tota in hoc sæculo vita, igne persecutionis, tribulationis, et paupertatis plena fuit, nec tamen vitiorum flamma incensus, et ab omni adversitate in resurrectione est erutus.
paras.en: [[3:2|And the Lord said|Et dixit Dominus]] Jesus [[3:2|to Satan: The Lord rebuke thee|ad Satan : Increpet Dominus in te]]. This Christ said and did when, the third temptation completed, he answered: [[Matt 4:10|Begone, Satan|Vade, Satana]]; it is written: [[Matt 4:7|Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God|Non tentabis Dominum Deum tuum]][[Deut 6:16||]] [Denis joins to the answer of the third temptation (Matt 4:10) that of the second (Matt 4:7), which quotes Deut 6:16]. For Christ called himself Lord, and he himself stirred himself up to rebuke Satan. [[3:2|Is not this a brand plucked out of the fire?|Numquid non iste torris est erutus de igne?]] This fits Christ most exactly, whose whole life in this world was full of the fire of persecution, of tribulation and of poverty; and yet he was not set alight by the flame of vices, and in the resurrection he was plucked out of all adversity.

paras.t: Et Jesus erat indutus vestibus sordidis, id est indetrahibilibus defectibus, quos pro nobis suscepit, sicut et Isaias testatur: Vidimus eum, et non erat adspectus; et reputavimus eum quasi leprosum, et percussum a Deo. Vere languores nostros ipse tulit, et dolores nostros ipse portavit. Ipse denique de suo corpore ait ad Patrem in Psalmo : Conscidisti saccum meum, et cumdedisti me lætitia. Teste etiam Paulo, ipse pro nobis factus est maledictum. Sed et tempore passionis vestes ejus adspersæ sunt sanguine, et ipse in Isaia protestatur: Omnia indumenta mea inquinavi. Hæc sordida vestimenta sunt a Christo tempore resurrectionis ablata, quando in corpore immortali impassibilique surrexit.
paras.en: [[3:3|And Jesus was clothed with filthy garments|Et Jesus erat indutus vestibus sordidis]], that is, with the blameless defects [defectus indetrahibiles: the penalties of our nature, such as hunger, weariness, suffering and death, which carry no sin or reproach] that he took upon himself for us, as Isaias too testifies: [[Is 53:2|we have seen him, and there was no sightliness|Vidimus eum, et non erat adspectus]]; and [[Is 53:4|we have thought him as it were a leper, and as one struck by God|reputavimus eum quasi leprosum, et percussum a Deo]]. [[Is 53:4|Surely he hath borne our infirmities and carried our sorrows|Vere languores nostros ipse tulit, et dolores nostros ipse portavit]]. Again, he himself says of his own body to the Father in the Psalm: [[Ps 29:12|thou hast cut my sackcloth, and hast compassed me with gladness|Conscidisti saccum meum, et cumdedisti me lætitia]]. Paul too bears witness that he was [[Gal 3:13|made a curse for us|pro nobis factus est maledictum]]. And moreover at the time of the passion his garments were sprinkled with blood, and he declares in Isaias: [[Is 63:3|I have stained all my apparel|Omnia indumenta mea inquinavi]]. These filthy garments were taken away from Christ at the time of the resurrection, when he rose in an immortal and impassible body.

paras.t: Et dixit ad eum angelus, id est ipse ad se ipsum ratione corporis sui mystici : Ecce abstuli a te iniquitatem tuam, id est tuorum : juxta id in Psalmo : Deus, tu scis insipientiam meam, et delicta mea a te non sunt abscondita. Dominus enim posuit in eo iniquitatem omnium nostrum. Et indui te mutatoriis, id est dotibus corporis glorificati in resurrectione, scilicet impassibilitate, agilitate, claritate, ac subtilitate. Christus nempe ut Deus suscitavit se ipsum, et corpus suum glorificavit, juxta quod ait in Evangelio S. Joannis : Solvite templum hoc, et in tribus diebus excitabo illud. Hoc autem dixit de templo corporis sui.
paras.en: [[3:4|And he said to him|Et dixit ad eum]], the angel, that is, he himself to himself, by reason of his mystical body: [[3:4|Behold I have taken away thy iniquity|Ecce abstuli a te iniquitatem tuam]], that is, the iniquity of thine own: in keeping with that in the Psalm: [[Ps 68:6|O God, thou knowest my foolishness; and my offences are not hidden from thee|Deus, tu scis insipientiam meam, et delicta mea a te non sunt abscondita]]. For [[Is 53:6|the Lord hath laid on him the iniquity of us all|Dominus enim posuit in eo iniquitatem omnium nostrum]]. [[3:4|And have clothed thee with change of garments|Et indui te mutatoriis]], that is, with the endowments of the glorified body in the resurrection, namely impassibility, agility, clarity and subtlety [the four dotes, or gifts, of the risen body in scholastic theology]. For Christ as God raised himself up and glorified his body, according to what he says in the Gospel of St. John: [[John 2:19|Destroy this temple; and in three days I will raise it up|Solvite templum hoc, et in tribus diebus excitabo illud]]. [[John 2:21|But he spoke of the temple of his body|Hoc autem dixit de templo corporis sui]].

paras.t: Ponite cidarim, id est divinæ majestatis splendorem, super caput ejus. Sed quomodo angeli jubentur hoc facere, vel sordida vestimenta a Christo auferre, nisi quantum ad manifestationem? Cooperati sunt enim glorificationi Christi, in cordibus hominum ejus notitiam hominibus revelando, et ita induerunt eum vestibus in cognitione credentium. Sic namque et Christus perhibet se Patrem clarificasse : Ego, inquiens, te clarificavi super terram.
paras.en: [[3:5|Put a clean mitre|Ponite cidarim]] [Denis leaves out mundam, "clean"], that is, the splendour of the divine majesty, [[3:5|upon his head|super caput ejus]]. But how are the angels bidden to do this, or to take the filthy garments away from Christ, except as regards making it known? For they cooperated in the glorification of Christ by revealing the knowledge of him to men in their hearts, and so [[3:5|clothed him with garments|induerunt eum vestibus]] in the knowledge of believers. For so Christ too declares that he glorified the Father: [[John 17:4|I|Ego]], he says, [[John 17:4|have glorified thee on the earth|te clarificavi super terram]].

paras.t: Præterea quod subditur, quemadmodum angelus contestatus est Jesum, dicens, Hæc dicit Dominus, Si in viis meis ambulaveris, etc., judicabis domum meam, refertur ad mysticum ejus corpus. Audi, Jesu sacerdos magne, tu et amici tui, id est Apostoli ac viri perfecti; ecce ego adducam servum meum Orientem, id est te ipsum secundum naturam humanam, ad explenda universa humanæ salutis mysteria.
paras.en: Further, what follows, how the angel [[3:6|protested to Jesus, saying|contestatus est Jesum, dicens]]: [[3:7|Thus saith the Lord|Hæc dicit Dominus]]: [[3:7|If thou wilt walk in my ways|Si in viis meis ambulaveris]], etc., thou [[3:7|shalt judge my house|judicabis domum meam]], refers to his mystical body. [[3:8|Hear, O Jesus thou high priest, thou and thy friends|Audi, Jesu sacerdos magne, tu et amici tui]], that is, the Apostles and perfect men; [[3:8|behold, I WILL BRING MY SERVANT THE ORIENT|ecce ego adducam servum meum Orientem]], that is, thyself according to thy human nature, to accomplish all the mysteries of man's salvation.

paras.t: Moraliter autem, ostendit Dominus Zachariæ, id est viro perfecto Dei jugiter recordanti, Jesum sacerdotem magnum, id est quemcumque aliorum prælatum sive episcopum, cujus est aliorum cooperari saluti, stantem coram angelo, qui custos est animæ ejus. Satan vero non cessat talibus adversari; sed Deus noster pugnat pro nobis, et per angelicos spiritus, dæmonum impugnationem coercet a nobis, conteritque Satanam sub pedibus nostris velociter. Hujusmodi autem sacerdos propter sollicitudinem et laborem, ceterasque propter justitiam persecutiones quas habet in regimine pastorali, recte assimilatur torris eruto de igne. Ideo Dominus non permittit eum supra id quod potest, tentari, sed opem impendit, faciens cum tentatione proventum.
paras.en: Morally, however, [[3:1|the Lord shewed|ostendit Dominus]] to Zacharias, that is, to the perfect man who is ever mindful of God [the name Zacharias was taken to mean "remembrance of the Lord"], [[3:1|Jesus the high priest|Jesum sacerdotem magnum]], that is, any prelate over others, or bishop, whose office it is to cooperate in the salvation of others, [[3:1|standing before the angel|stantem coram angelo]] who is the guardian of his soul. Satan, indeed, does not cease to be the adversary of such men; but our God fights for us, and through the angelic spirits holds back from us the assaults of the demons, and crushes Satan under our feet speedily[[Rom 16:20||]]. Now such a priest, because of the care and toil, and the other persecutions for justice' sake, which he bears in pastoral government, is rightly likened to [[3:2|a brand plucked out of the fire|torris eruto de igne]]. Therefore the Lord does not suffer him to be tempted above that which he is able, but gives him help, making with temptation issue[[1 Cor 10:13||]].

paras.t: Iste insuper est indutus vestibus sordidis. Justus enim septies in die cadit; sed ministerio angelorum, et inspiratione eorum purgatur ac pœnitet; mutatoriisque vestitur, id est donis et gratiis Spiritus Sancti. Sed et cidaris ponitur super caput ejus, id est dignitas Ordinis sacerdotalis dispositive ab angelis, a quibus electi diriguntur, secundum præordinationem divinam ad sacerdotii Christi susceptionem: sicque induitur vestimentis virtutum, et gratia sacramentali quæ in susceptione Ordinis sacerdotalis confertur.
paras.en: Moreover this man is [[3:3|clothed with filthy garments|indutus vestibus sordidis]]. For [[Prov 24:16|a just man shall fall seven times|Justus enim septies in die cadit]] a day [Denis quotes Prov 24:16 in its common form, "seven times a day"]; but by the ministry of the angels and by their inspiration he is cleansed and does penance, and is clothed with [[3:4|change of garments|mutatoriisque vestitur]], that is, with the gifts and graces of the Holy Ghost. And the [[3:5|mitre|cidaris]] too is put [[3:5|upon his head|super caput ejus]], that is, the dignity of the priestly Order, dispositively [that is, the angels prepare and dispose him, while God gives the Order itself] by the angels, by whom the elect are directed, according to the divine preordination, to the receiving of the priesthood of Christ: and so he is clothed with the garments of the virtues, and with the sacramental grace that is conferred in receiving the priestly Order.

paras.t: Denique hujuscemodi sacerdotem sive pontificem Dominus contestatur: Si in viis meis ambulaveris, tu quoque judicabis domum meam, id est, congregationem fidelium tibi commissam sapienter discuties, discernes ac reges, atque in sacerdotii tui officio salubriter permanebis. Datque ei Deus omnipotens angelorum subsidium, qui sibi in subditorum custodia et salute fideliter cooperentur. Hinc insuper Dominus ait: Ecce adducam servum meum Orientem, id est, Christum tibi adesse faciam in Sacramento, et in medio loquentium de ipso ex caritate. Sed et Pater et Filius ad fideles veniendo, mansionem in ipsis efficiunt gratiosam.
paras.en: Lastly, the Lord solemnly charges such a priest or bishop: [[3:7|If thou wilt walk in my ways|Si in viis meis ambulaveris]], [[3:7|thou also shalt judge my house|tu quoque judicabis domum meam]], that is, thou shalt wisely examine, discern and govern the congregation of the faithful committed to thee, and shalt abide to good effect in the office of thy priesthood. And almighty God gives him the help of the angels, to work faithfully with him in the guarding and the salvation of those under him. Hence the Lord says moreover: [[3:8|behold, I WILL BRING MY SERVANT THE ORIENT|Ecce adducam servum meum Orientem]], that is, I will make Christ present to thee in the Sacrament, and in the midst of those who speak of him out of charity[[Matt 18:20||]]. And indeed the Father and the Son, coming to the faithful, make a gracious abode in them[[John 14:23||]].
